quests.title: The White Curtain Falls

dialogue.t: It sure is cold today. I wonder how much heavier the snow's gonna get...
Here to see Odette? I just need to see your tickets for the preview.
...Perfect, thank you. I'll hold onto your tickets. Come on in, it's freezing outside.

dialogue.sit: (I think I'll leave the Lelek question until after the show's over. Then, I'll go find Odette.)
(Childe said he was originally going to come with Tonia... So I'm guessing Tonia's already here somewhere.)
(Is there anyone here who looks like a Tonia...? Let's see, it's a small audience — makes sense for a preview... But wait, I do see some familiar faces...)
(Mr. Chugunov's back again, by the looks of it. Oh, and is that Mitya? And that Fatui officer, Valeriy... Guess he must be playing cat-and-mouse with Mitya again.)
(Oh no, it looks like the show's starting, and I still haven't found Tonia... Never mind. I'll just have to take a seat for now and see if I can catch her afterwards.)

dialogue.t: (Applause)
Hello, members of the audience. I'm a staff member here at the theater.
Today's performance was a very special one for us, as it marks the first attempt in a long time to revive the classic Snezhnayan ballet, "Spirit Seeker."
To commemorate this occasion, we would love to take a group photo of the cast, crew, and audience members present today. Could I kindly ask the audience to please come up onto the stage...
Alright, everyone huddle in a little more... Now look at the camera... One, two, three!
Are you quite satisfied, Mr. Energy Scientist? I rather hope you don't have any other escape plans to add to my workload today.
Haha, what are you talking about, Sarge? This was simply my way of inviting you to watch Miss Odette's new show with me.
And wasn't the performance spectacular? In the future, I heartily encourage you to take a leaf out of my book — find some soul-nourishing pastimes to enrich your time outside of work.
It was indeed a fine performance. But I must correct you on one point — this is not "time outside of work." These are working hours.
Eh, working hours and non-working hours are just a social construct. Human technology can never advance if we're too rigid in our thinking, Sarge.
May we leave now?
Already? I mean, I was kinda hoping to soak up the atmosphere for a little longer, but... No? Okay, guess I'm pushing my luck... Didn't seem like too much to ask, but fair enough...
Off we go then, Sarge. Back to the land of "working hours." Lead the way.

dialogue.sit: (...That has to be her. She's the only person in the audience around Tonia's age.)
Excuse me... are you Tonia?

dialogue.t: Huh...?

dialogue.sit: Your brother's busy today, so I took his ticket. Don't worry about him, he's fine.

dialogue.t: Oh, okay. Sorry for the trouble.
*cough*... *cough*...

dialogue.sit: What's wrong? Are you sick?

dialogue.t: *cough*... No, I'm fine, it's nothing...

dialogue.sit: (Maybe she caught a cold on the way here because of the weather?)

dialogue.t: ...I haven't seen snow like this in a long, long time. It's most unusual.
I know, it's completely white out there — you can barely see a thing. I've never seen such heavy snow in my life.
Let's wait it out for now. You'd be lucky not to freeze to death in this weather, let alone find your way.
Well, look at that. Maybe we shouldn't be in such a rush to get back after all. What do you think?
...Let's wait and see.
Ugh, why do you need to take it so seriously? Fate has given us this wonderful chance to take a break. We owe it to ourselves to make the most of it.
Come to think of it, there's a small inn not far from here that always keeps plenty of extra blankets on hand for guests.
I know the route well. Shall I head over and borrow a few blankets? That way, anyone in a hurry can wrap up warm for the journey back. Just remember to return them next time you're over this way.
Sir, there's really no need to go to all that trouble...
Hey, it's no trouble at all. Wait here, I'll be right back.
What a kind gentleman. Very good — my wife and daughter are waiting for me at home, so I shall be heading back as soon as I get my blanket.
Um, so... are you expecting us to go back to the Armory Palace wrapped in blankets, too?

Don't worry about that. I made arrangements in advance: Should I not return to the Armory Palace within three and a half hours after Operation Showtime begins, an armed squad will be sent to collect us.
They will escort us back. You are one of our key military personnel, so any weather-related risks must be eliminated.
Operation Showtime...? So wait, every single time you drag me back to work when I sneak out, it's a whole official operation?
I gotta say, you've really turned this into quite a moral dilemma for me...

dialogue.sit: It's snowing pretty hard out there. I think you should stay here for now. You seem a little under the weather.

dialogue.t: Sure. My brother might come pick me up in a bit anyway.

dialogue.sit: (Time to get to work... I should head backstage and find Odette. I need to look her in the eye and ask her about Lelek.)

dialogue.t: Excuse me, are you looking for someone?

dialogue.sit: I'm looking for Odette.
I'm looking for Vodyanitsa.
I'm looking for Alyosha.

dialogue.t: Ah. A fan, I'm guessing? Today's just a dress rehearsal, so Miss Odette won't be meeting with fans. She's taking a well-earned rest right now.
Sorry, but that area is currently off-limits to everyone except the cast and crew.

dialogue.sit: (Huh, bad timing, I guess... Well, I might as well stick around. I doubt Odette will be leaving before the snow lets up in any case.)
An hour goes by, but the snowstorm shows no sign of stopping...

dialogue.t: What happened to the gentleman who went to fetch the blankets? How has he still not returned?
I was thinking the same thing. It's still snowing very hard. Do you think something might have happened to him?
Whatever the reason for his delay, I must say, I hate nothing more than people who make empty promises and fail to deliver.
Well, I have to treat my employees like that on occasion, but that's different...
You seem anxious, Mr. Valeriy.
It's been nearly four hours since I left the Armory. The army should have arrived to extract us by now.
They know how much I despise tardiness and disrupted plans... There's simply no reason that they shouldn't have shown up by now, barring exceptional circumstances.
Surely a snowstorm like this one counts as such?
Few things in this world can stop the Snezhnayan army, Mr. Mitya, and a snowstorm is certainly not one of them.
Why don't you go out and take a look? They might be right outside, waiting for your orders before they dare come in.
An absurd hypothesis. I have no intention of leaving your side for even a moment until I have escorted you back to the Armory Palace.
This doesn't look like an ordinary snowstorm to me...
That guy who left earlier... it looked like he just vanished into thin air. Either that, or my eyes were playing tricks on me...
A "man-eating snowstorm"? Come on, night hasn't even fallen yet. Spare us the ghost stories.
{NICKNAME}. Didn't know you were coming today. How come you didn't say anything?

dialogue.sit: I'm here to see Odette.
(I'm not sure how I should say this...)

dialogue.t: Oh right. I assumed you were looking for me and Vodyanitsa. Odette's still backstage.
Whoa, that's quite a snowstorm out there... I've been working backstage this whole time, so I didn't even notice. No wonder the audience hasn't left yet.

dialogue.sit: Is weather like this rare even in Snezhnaya?

dialogue.t: Yeah. Snow like this... I'm sure I've seen it out in the wild before, but never in the city.
Actually... I take that back — I don't think I've seen snow this bad even in the wild. This is... something else. It's not normal.

dialogue.sit: (If even Alyosha thinks snow like this isn't normal... could it have anything to do with that monster people have been talking about?)

dialogue.t: We can't stay cooped up here forever. Someone needs to go out and take a look.

dialogue.sit: Should I go with you?

dialogue.t: No need. I have plenty of experience with snowstorms. Besides, I work here, while you're an audience member. I should be the one to do it.
Everyone by the door, careful not to let the snow soak into your shoes. In a snowstorm, you gotta look after your toes above all else.
Heading out, my man? Be careful. I've been told this snowstorm eats people alive.
Thanks for the advice. I am planning to be careful. I just wanna take a quick look at the situation out there.
Phew...
He's back, he's back! How was it? What's going on out there?
Did you see any soldiers patrolling the area?
...Something about this storm isn't right.
There's no one out there — I didn't see a single soul. And something in the air gives me the creeps.
This isn't your average snowstorm. I suspect it might be related to recent events in our nation. I strongly advise everyone to stay here until the snow dies down.
Are you serious? So all of us are trapped here now? That sounds a little far-fetched to me...
You wanna go outside and see? I, for one, am not risking my neck in that weather.
This just turned from a minor delay into a major hassle.
We can only hope that our friend who went to fetch the blankets just ditched us and went home.
Is it really that bad? But my daughter... I won't be able to read her a bedtime story tonight...
Huh? What are you all still doing here...?
Whoa! It's snowing hard...

dialogue.sit: The cast and crew from backstage are quickly brought up to date on the situation...

dialogue.t: So now we're stuck here? This is terrible... Luckily, it was just a dress rehearsal today, so there aren't too many people here...
On the bright side, the theater's always well stocked with supplies. If the snow still doesn't let up as we get into the evening, you can spend the night here, everyone.
At least, I assume that's alright? Odette?
Fine by me.
This seems like a sensible backup plan under the circumstances. My thanks to the theater for being so accommodating.
What are you staring outside and praying for, my man? You anxious to get home too?
O, Your Majesty the Tsaritsa, I beg you, please do not let tonight's snowstorm stop...
...This is a golden opportunity to spend the night under the same roof as the two top stars in all of Snezhnaya! It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience!
I think I've changed my mind.
Sir, if you so much as look at us funny, you'll be seeing stars in a whole other way. Behave yourself, or you'll be begging for that blizzard.
It's getting colder. We need to keep the indoor temperature up.
Close the door and lock it tight. Let's head somewhere warmer.
I have to say, even though today was a rehearsal and there were some hiccups along the way, Miss Odette's performance was one of the best I've ever seen! Even compared to an actual show!
I couldn't agree more! Especially considering the weight of the subject matter. It takes a truly seasoned professional to do justice to a theme like love and regret...
...Do you think we were coming on too strong? Odette's ignoring us again.
What about you? What did you think of today's performance?

dialogue.sit: Actually, I wasn't paying much attention.
I think you could be more expressive.
Consider me a new fan, Odette.

dialogue.t: Really? Hmm, that means it wasn't captivating enough to draw you in. I'll work harder to win you over next time.
I'll make sure to save a ticket for you when the show's performance-ready.

dialogue.sit: (This doesn't seem like the time or place to bring up the subject of Lelek. I need a chance to speak with her in private...)

dialogue.t: (...So unfair! Talk about double standards!)

dialogue.sit: (And now it looks like I've been spotted.)
You know Mitya too?

dialogue.t: No, I don't. I just... I have a feeling that he might be dangerous.
...Do you think we were coming on too strong? Odette's ignoring us again.
...This is highly irregular. A delay of over an hour during an operation like this theoretically warrants a Harbinger-level response. I wonder what the issue is... the storm, or something else...?
*sigh*... Sarge, the day you learn to let go and just enjoy moments like this is the day you'll finally understand the meaning of life.
Ah~ Why, hello, Sir(Ma'am). I believe you were the one sitting at a nearby table at Podvorye Restaurant?
Any friend of the theater's star performers is a friend of mine. It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm Mitya, from the Energy Commission.
Greetings. Major Valeriy, head of the Special Assignments Battalion, Armory Palace Royal Grenadier Guards, First Regiment.
I am here to ensure Mr. Mitya's personal safety. Please let me know if I can be of any assistance.

dialogue.sit: I'm {NICKNAME}.
Delighted to meet you both.

dialogue.t: Um... Mr.(Ms.) {NICKNAME}, I noticed that Miss Odette is stealing glances at me. Do you have any idea what it could be about?
I've racked my brains, but I can't think of anything I might have done to offend her... Perhaps she noticed me spacing out during her performance?

dialogue.sit: No idea...
Keep racking those brains. You'll figure it out.
So, Mr. Mitya, is your work related to Project Stuzha?

dialogue.t: Yes, that's right. The higher-ups in the Fatui transferred me from the Energy Commission to the Armory Palace because they wanted me to...
Really? I can't even talk about that? Pretty sure it counts as part of my private life...
Alright, alright, I won't say anything. *sigh* Sorry, {NICKNAME}. As you can see, I'm afraid this pleasant chat will have to end here.
...This is highly irregular. A delay of over an hour during an operation like this theoretically warrants a Harbinger-level response. I wonder what the issue is... the storm, or something else...?
I don't think it's ever been this lively backstage before! I didn't know you were coming today.
Hey, have you seen Chugunov? I heard he was coming today... Have you spoken to him at all?

dialogue.sit: Not really.

dialogue.t: I'm with you. This could be just the chance we need.
Yeah. I gotta figure out a way to coax some more intel out of him... I wanna know why he suddenly changed his stance on Project Stuzha. What exactly happened before the most recent Veche vote?
For the Rokot? Or just out of personal interest?
Shh...! There are other people around, don't say the R-word!
Shh...! There are other people around, don't say the R-word!

dialogue.sit: How are you feeling, Tonia?

dialogue.t: I'm fine. Sorry to worry you. I'm used to it by this point. I take medicine for it — my brother usually helps to get it ready for me.

dialogue.sit: (Childe must take great care of his sister. He's never mentioned Tonia's illness, though.)

dialogue.t: Y'know, I actually find this whole thing kind of exciting...
Stuck in a strange place thanks to a snowstorm, having to spend the night with a bunch of interesting characters... It's pretty cool, don't you think?

dialogue.sit: You're right. It's certainly a novel experience.
I'm sure most kids share that wish.

dialogue.t: Exactly! It's like... one of those stories where an ordinary school trip turns into a magical adventure. I've always wanted something like that to happen in real life.
*cough*... *cough*...
Oh, I'm fine, really. Just got a little overexcited.

dialogue.sit: Look after yourself — otherwise, your brother will come after me!

dialogue.t: *cough*... *cough*...
My husband has major trust issues... To him, I doubt even this snowstorm is a good enough excuse for me to stay out all night.
That's the price of marrying into wealth. You'll get used to it. I'm not about to stop you if you want to leave, but don't drag me along.
...Uh, hello? Can I help you?
...And then there's the aristocrats — easiest of all to deal with. You don't need to use any force whatsoever. All you have to do is show them the rope you plan to tie them up with. Do you know why?
I don't. Do tell...
Because nothing horrifies them more than the thought of a cheap, coarse rope leaving creases on their precious million-Mora coat. They'll do whatever you ask to avoid that fate.
Hahahaha... Unexpected, but funny nonetheless! Hahaha, tell me another one!
Well, look at that, I got myself a new listener. Hey there, lemme introduce myself. The name's Shram, and I'm a mercenary. The kind that gets paid to do odd jobs for rich folks.
And I am Chugunov, an entrepreneur. If my name is unfamiliar to you, you will no doubt have heard of my factory, the renowned Iskra Manufacturing Plant.

dialogue.sit: I'm {NICKNAME}.
Enjoy your conversation.

dialogue.t: Are you really that famous, Mr. Chugunov? How come I've never heard your name before?
E—Excuse me? ...I—Is that a joke, or are you being serious?
Oh, I'll have to ask my rope later. It's probably tied up more entrepreneurs than I've ever heard of.
Hahaha... Ahem...
E—Excuse me? ...I—Is that a joke, or are you being serious?

dialogue.sit: Time flies by as people make light-hearted conversation and gradually get to know one another. Before you know it, the evening grows late...

dialogue.t: How's it looking, Alyosha?
No change from this afternoon. Heavy snow with no sign of slowing down.
Ahem! May I have your attention, please. The storm is unlikely to stop tonight, and it'll be even more dangerous outside at night than it was during the day.
We at the theater owe everyone here a duty of care. Therefore, we strongly suggest that you stay on site overnight and avoid going outside unless absolutely necessary.
In a few short moments, we'll give you a tour of the theater's various quarters. You can choose to sleep in the VIP room, the office, or backstage. ...Or on the stage, if you'd prefer. We won't mind.
I'll pass on sleeping on the stage. What if the snow has stopped by tomorrow morning? The early-birds in the audience might think we're part of some experimental new show.
A drama about sleeping? Hah, that could be fun. Maybe we should come up with a title for the production.

dialogue.sit: "Sleeping Beauty"?
"The Slumbering Heavenly Principles"?

dialogue.t: Not bad! Clear selling point, at least. Could be a big hit!
Anyone who doesn't wish to sleep on the stage, please follow me. I'll show you to the rooms.

dialogue.sit: (I guess I'll call it a night... Though I feel like I won't sleep very well without Paimon here.)
(I'm sure she'll be worried that I haven't made it back yet. But as long as she looks out the window, she'll probably realize what's holding me up.)
(I wonder if she's feeling any better yet? At least she hasn't been getting any worse... Still, I should try and get back first thing tomorrow morning.)

dialogue.t: Ah, finally. Welcome back to the world of the living, lazybones. I was about to wake you. The black mist is almost on us.

dialogue.sit: What "black mist"?
Where are we?

dialogue.t: Hmm? Still waking up, huh? You know — the black mist. It's been chasing us from below ever since we were born. You're just dozy, there's no way you've forgotten.
C'mon, let's keep heading up. Onwards and upwards is the only way to survive — don't listen to a word those black mist cultists say.
*sigh* Here we go again... The endless march toward survival...

dialogue.sit: (What's going on? That black mist down there is creeping me out, and it's rising... Guess I should head upwards and get away from it...)

dialogue.t: Torgov and Soboleva are gone... I never thought the day would come when even they would be swallowed by the black mist. It's just you and me now.

dialogue.sit: Is it just me, or has the black mist stopped moving?

dialogue.t: Yes. It looks like it's satisfied — for now.
This happens from time to time. But it won't be long before the black mist starts chasing survivors once again. No one knows how to stop its advance for good.
Well, we should make the most of the precious moments of rest that those two bought for us...
Huh? Are you really that sleepy, {NICKNAME}?
I... I can't do this anymore. I've had enough of being forever on the run... What's the point of it all?
All this will pass eventually, I promise. Keep fighting. It will be worth it.
You accuse the black mist cultists of being liars, but you're lying too. There is no end to this path — it keeps going up forever. There was never any hope to begin with!
The cult of the black mist has poisoned your mind, Soboleva. Are you thinking of giving up as well?
I am. I think I'll take my chances with the black mist over this perpetual torture.
As much as I detest the black mist cultists, I'm just too weary...
Then I bid you both farewell. Let me put my personal opinions aside for a moment and say: I hope that you both find peace within the black mist.

dialogue.sit: So we're just gonna give up on them?

dialogue.t: Fate always appears so impossibly complicated. But at moments like this, its raw simplicity is laid bare.
Their fate was sealed from the instant they entertained doubt. From then on, the outcome was both inevitable and irreversible... Let's go.

quests.description: You suspect Odette of being Lelek. To be sure of the truth and obtain more intel, you go to the Korolevskiy Theater to take part in a test performance. During this time, the blizzard that sweeps across Snezhnograd seems to grow ever stronger…

quests.title: Lelek's Confession

dialogue.t: Aaaaah!!! Help! Somebody, come quick!!!
What is it, Chugunov? What's wrong— Huh!?

dialogue.sit: (...Is it morning already? What's all the commotion?)
(Sounds like it's coming from next door. I should check and see what's going on.)

dialogue.t: Don't look, Miss Tonia, stay here...
O—Okay...
What happened to them?
Two people are lying down in the room, completely still, as if they're still asleep.
But your gut tells you that they are not sleeping. Somehow, you can sense it in your bones. This is what death looks like.

dialogue.sit: (These two people have passed away... And the strange thing is that somehow, I knew this was going to happen. I knew that they would be the ones to die...)
(Have I seen this moment before? Or did I have some kind of premonition? I can't remember what it was...)

dialogue.t: Let me take a look.
...No vital signs in either of them. They're dead.
The cause of death, however, remains unclear. No wounds on the bodies, no signs of a struggle, and no skin discoloration caused by the buildup of toxins...
But just last night, they were chatting and joking away... This is so sudden...
Could they have had pre-existing medical conditions...? Hmm... Even then, the odds of them both dying of sudden complications on the same night are extremely low...
It's hard to believe that they died of natural causes, nor does this appear to be suicide.

dialogue.sit: Are you suggesting... they were murdered?

dialogue.t: Who was the first to discover the bodies?
Ah, I... I—It was me... But these deaths have nothing to do with me, Officer. I got up early, because I wanted to see if the snow had stopped...
Then I noticed that the door to this room was open, and it looked like there was a man and woman inside... I just went over to see what was going on — I had no idea they were... they were...
I can corroborate this. I was doing my morning exercises near the stage. When I saw Mr. Chugunov heading this way, I followed him.
I can also confirm that I didn't see a single person approach that room before him.
The snowstorm was raging all night, and it's still going now. There's no way someone could have come in from outside, correct?
You mean, an intruder? No, not possible. I slept by the door last night as a precaution. There's no way I wouldn't have noticed if anyone had tried to open it.
Everyone, split into pairs and search the theater for anyone in hiding or any signs of suspicious activity. I'll follow up with a full search of my own shortly. Go, there's no time to waste!

dialogue.sit: You pair up with Tonia. After a thorough search, you're satisfied that no one else from outside the group is in the theater, and everything is exactly as it was left last night.

dialogue.t: ...Nothing on your end either?
Backstage is clear. No signs of suspicious activity.
We checked the basement — also clear. I don't think there's anywhere here that a living person could hide.

dialogue.sit: I didn't find anything either.

dialogue.t: Are we certain that the theater doesn't have a back door? Or any tunnel or passageway wide enough for a person to fit through?
No, there's nothing like that. If people were sneaking in through some secret tunnel to avoid buying a ticket, we'd have sealed it off ages ago.
I also checked the windows. All of them are locked from the inside, and there's no sign of anyone entering or leaving.
Sounds like we can safely rule out the intruder theory. If anyone came in during the night in this weather, there'd be no way for them to avoid leaving footprints or water stains.
This can only mean one thing... It's like one of those murder mysteries you see in novels and plays, isn't it? The ones where the killer is... one of us.
We can't quite jump to that conclusion just yet.

dialogue.sit: (Could he be right? It's hard to imagine something like that happening in real life...)
(Set in a theater during a snowstorm... a murder takes place, and the killer is among us... It's such a classic trope that it seems unbelievable.)

dialogue.t: Looking at who the killer targeted, and the clean entry and exit...
Hmph, it all adds up. I know what this is. It's obvious now that I think about it...
What is? What have you figured out?
Both victims were wealthy, well-known local merchants... and the door was deliberately left open, so I would discover the bodies and witness the crime scene first thing in the morning...
Such ruthless methods... This was your doing, wasn't it... Lelek?
Lelek!?
You mean, Lelek is among us? And he's the killer?
Lelek... I know this codename. Member of the Rokot, anti–Project Stuzha, always works alone. I've read the case files at the Armory Palace.
Walk me through your reasoning, Mr. Chugunov. What do you know about Lelek?
What now, huh? What now, Lelek? What more do you want from me? I already voted against Project Stuzha at the Snezhnograd Veche!
You snuck into my house the other day while I was asleep... left a threatening letter... And I did all that you asked! But Project Stuzha cannot be so easily shaken. Not with The Rooster in charge...
(So he really was threatened by Lelek. That makes sense.)
And now you're resorting to murder to threaten me. Isn't that right? I knew it. The Rokot despises the rich. The lives of the wealthy are but refuse in your eyes...
Show yourself! Which one of you is Lelek, hmm? Tell me! I'll... I'll do whatever you want. Just stop playing these mind games!

dialogue.sit: (Was this really Lelek's doing? Would Odette really do something like this?)
(If Odette really is Lelek, this seems out of character. But then again... How well do I really know her?)
(I'm probably the only one here with a compelling theory about Lelek's true identity. But if I reveal it now, I'll be putting Odette in the line of fire...)
(What should I do?)

dialogue.t: I don't think it's likely that Lelek killed anyone.
At least from the stories I've heard, he's never killed anyone before, and his name has never come up in connection with any murder cases.
Besides... even if Lelek did want to threaten you, why resort to such an extreme and roundabout method? It's not his style at all.

dialogue.sit: (Vodyanitsa doesn't know that Lelek might be Odette, but her assessment is pretty much identical to mine.)

dialogue.t: Miss Vodyanitsa... Why do you suddenly feel the need to speak in Lelek's defense?
Defense? Oh, no, no, it's just... I'm worried that we're jumping to conclusions here, so I wanted to share my point of view. Also... I don't think the Rokot is as bad as you're making it out to be.
n/a
Well, if you think I'm so wrong, what's your theory then, hmm? Why don't you tell us who the killer is?
The case is still evolving, Mr. Chugunov. Please do not prevent others from expressing their opinions so early on in the discussion.
Even so, there's no denying that the recent threat received by Mr. Chugunov may well be an important clue...
So there's still a good chance that Lelek is right here among us?
Ugh, I can't do this anymore. I don't care if it's still snowing outside — I have to get out of here...
Whoa, take a beat. We all know it's far too dangerous out there — even the soldiers couldn't get to us. Go out that door, and you might not live to tell the tale.
And whoever this "Lelek" is, they're surely not going to murder anyone in broad daylight. Be sensible, my man. You're safer inside.
As much as I regret having to say this, I'd like everyone to cooperate and refrain from exiting the premises until further notice.
Because as things stand... every one of us is now a suspect.
Unless anyone has further information to share, let's adjourn for now. Feel free to keep searching for clues, but make sure you don't go off alone.
...You're right, that was my bad. It was a knee-jerk reaction — I didn't think it through. Luckily, no one suspected my identity.

dialogue.sit: Hello.

dialogue.t: Aah! Oh, phew... It's just you. I thought someone was eavesdropping.

dialogue.sit: (Since Vodyanitsa and I were on the same page earlier, I think I should share my thoughts with the Rokot members first...)
You tell Vodyanitsa and Alyosha about Childe's intel on Lelek and your views on the current situation...

dialogue.t: Whoa, whoa, whoa... Are you serious? I dunno if this counts as "gossip," but it's definitely on track to be the juiciest this whole year...
Odette... Really, Odette? Oh god, how dumb does this make me look? Lelek has been right under my nose this whole time, and I didn't notice a thing...
Actually, it's exactly what you'd expect. Sometimes, hiding in plain sight is the best strategy.
Mm... And now that you mention it, the more I think about it, the more sense it seems to make. It all adds up...
What are we up to now...? One, two, three... four...

dialogue.sit: What are you counting?

dialogue.t: Odette's identities. She's my coworker — specifically a ballerina — and also a Fatuus, a member of the Rokot, now Lelek...
It must be so exhausting. I just want to give her a hug.
I guess since I've always known her as a member of the Fatui, it never even crossed my mind that she could be involved with the Rokot. Let alone being Lelek...
I don't understand. If she's with the Fatui, what reason could she have for being so opposed to Project Stuzha?
Probably best if you ask her that in person.
Well, since you waited until now to bring this up instead of announcing it to everyone earlier... does that mean we're all on the same page here?

dialogue.sit: She doesn't seem like the type to kill innocent people.

dialogue.t: Yeah. Lelek may not follow orders from the Rokot leadership, but as far as I'm concerned, she's never crossed the line. If anything, her actions benefit the poor.
...We need to confront her face-to-face.
Do you think she'd really admit to being Lelek?
I don't know. We'll have to see how it goes. For now, we'll work on the assumption that she didn't kill anyone and see how much she's willing to tell us.
Now's our chance — Odette's alone... Let's go!
Hey, Odette...
Hmm? What is it, you guys?
Shh... keep your voice down. We... need to talk.
So, um... you... You're Lelek, aren't you?
Alright, fine, you don't have to say anything or explain yourself, just... hear me out first.
None of us believes you'd kill innocent people. Whoever murdered those two people last night, it wasn't you.
{NICKNAME} was the first to figure out your identity, but he(she) kept quiet during the discussion just now.
Still, it's clear where the group consensus is heading. Everyone believes Lelek is the culprit. If your identity is exposed, you'll be in a really bad spot...
We're your colleagues, and we know what kind of person you are. I don't want anything bad to happen to you.
So... can you clue us in? Tell us everything. The more we know, the more easily we'll be able to cover for you...
Alright.
Yes, I'm Lelek, and no, I'm not the murderer.
And thanks, but I don't need you to cover for me. Actually... I'm planning to reveal my identity.
Huh? You're gonna reveal that you're Lelek? Here!?
That's right. I'll admit, I was surprised at first when Chugunov guessed that I was here. It was just a lucky guess, but it caught me off guard.
But after taking some time to assess the situation and confirm where everyone stands, I don't believe I have anything to worry about.
Are you sure you don't need a second opinion...? Given the circumstances...
Phew... Mr. Valeriy!
Whaaat!?
You seem to be very comfortable taking charge, Major. You took the reins as soon as things went south.
I simply made an executive decision that someone needed to take control of this situation on the military's behalf. Does this offend you?
No, quite the opposite. We feel much safer for it. By the way, what does "Major" mean, exactly? Is it a pretty high rank?
I still find it hard to believe there's a murderer among us... Just last night, I imagined we were like classmates out on a hiking trip...
There's no guarantee that you can trust your classmates. Especially not when you're locked up together.
*sigh* Why did they do this? Was it for money? Even then, they could have just kidnapped the people. They didn't have to die...
We don't move in the same circles, so I'm not clued up on "Project Stuzha" and all this political intrigue, nor does it interest me...
...Nevertheless, Sir, I think your top priority as soon as you get out of here should be to hire a good private bodyguard.
Such as... yourself?
Such as myself.

dialogue.sit: Valeriy gets everyone to reconvene. Odette gets straight to the point and announces that she is Lelek.

dialogue.t: So... Odette is Lelek...?
I don't know what game you're playing, but you've got a lot of nerve...
It's just one identity. So what if it's exposed? I can disappear and adopt a new identity anytime I please.
I made my peace with this when I chose to become Lelek.
But more importantly, I promise I am not the murderer... Which means that someone else is.
So if anyone still insists that I did this, you'd best produce the evidence now...

Otherwise, I suggest that you bite your tongue. Because if you really believe I killed two people without making a sound or leaving a trace... pointing fingers at me would surely only make you my next target.
Is this really the truth, Miss Odette?
Hmm, that's confidence all right. I believe you.

dialogue.sit: (A real no-nonsense attitude... I can see why Marionette said that she's on track to inherit the title of "The Fair Lady"...)

dialogue.t: Are you seriously buying this? Hey, Officer, she just admitted to being Lelek. Aren't you going to do something about this?
I do have one question... Miss Odette, why have you chosen this moment to come forward and reveal your identity?
...If I didn't say anything, everyone would be focusing all their efforts on finding Lelek.
And that is exactly what the real culprit wants. I don't want to be the scapegoat who lets the murderer get away with this crime.
Despite all the accusations, she made the smart choice... A remarkable display of rational thinking under pressure. Clearly, Odette's talent extends far beyond the art of dance.
She thought so far ahead... Ugh, why do I always feel like I'm one step behind her in everything...
...You've convinced me. Dealing with the murder case remains the top priority right now. Let's put the name "Lelek" and all related incidents aside until further notice.
Nevertheless, the group still considers you the prime suspect. I assume you have no quarrel with that, Miss Odette?
I understand. You're welcome to keep an eye on me around the clock. I have no objections.
Mr. Chugunov?

Hmph, for my wife and daughter's sake, I'll let you off the hook for now... But don't think you're forgiven for breaking into my house and threatening me... Just wait till we get out of here, Lelek. We'll settle the score then.

dialogue.sit: The snowstorm rages on. By now, everyone seems resigned to it. No further progress is made on the case, and before long, night falls...

dialogue.t: Good work, Lelek guard team. And Lelek too. Here, have some hot water.

dialogue.sit: (*sigh* Turns out Valeriy knew about my "exploits," so now I've been told I have to guard Lelek with him...)

dialogue.t: Shouldn't you be facing my way if you're guarding me? At the moment... It looks more like you're my bodyguards.
If the true culprit is indeed still at large, as you have claimed, we must keep our guard up against them also.
Don't worry, Tonia. We'll get through this.
Once the snow stops, the officials will step in, the investigation will get easier, and then we'll be safe.
Hmm... but once the snow stops, won't everyone just leave?
Hmm? You're gonna miss us, huh? Well... some of us work at the theater, so we'll still be here! I'll even give you a special backstage pass!
Really, Miss Vodyanitsa? That's awesome! You've made a fan for life!
Aw... You're so cute, Tonia.
Alright, let's swear to it! I promise to give you the pass, and you... you promise to never change your mind about being my fan!
Promise!
*sigh*... Don't indulge her, Tonia. You don't have to swear an oath over things like that...
You really do get carried away sometimes, don't you, Miss Vodyanitsa...
Hey! Mind your own business!
Hahaha...
Don't be nervous, Miss Water Imp. Everyone's here. There's nothing to be afraid of.
Excuse me? Do I look nervous? Don't be ridiculous...
Hm? No, no, no — you sound nervous, lass.
Ohh... Wait, but how... okay, plenty of people know that I'm a Water Imp, but still... How come you understand our primary mode of expression?
"Primary mode of expression"? I've not come across that concept before. Do enlighten me, Vodyanitsa.
Well, it's just... We Water Imps tend to communicate our emotions to each other by singing rather than with facial expressions.
The emotions we convey through song take precedence over our facial expressions. So, we think of it as our primary mode of expression.
I'm impressed, Shram. I didn't take you for a man of culture, but you're clearly rather learned.
It's not about being cultured or not... The thing is, this mode of expression can usually only be understood by other Water Imps. It's not a simple case of a song sounding happy or sad.
...And yet, you're clearly human, Mr. Shram.

It's really not the big deal you're making it out to be. I think I just have a knack for it. Plus, I have a... Hmm... very close friend who's a Water Imp. A delightful lady, hehe. But keep that a secret.
Anyway, we've spent so much time together that before I knew it, I noticed I could understand her expressions.
Oh. I guess that makes sense. Still, the fact that you have a Water Imp friend is even more surprising... Heh... I'd better watch what I'm singing when I'm around you from now on...
Hey... What are you implying? You're not... secretly insulting the audience in your songs, are you?
Heavens, why would I do a thing like that?
*yawn*...
It's getting late. We should discuss our sleeping arrangements for tonight. To guard against the killer, someone needs to keep watch.
I suggest that we don't sleep in separate quarters tonight. It will be safer if we all stay together.
Hmph, as long as someone keeps an eye on Lelek, I'm quite sure we won't have any trouble.
Are you saying that you wish to bet your life on Miss Odette being the killer?
I... Nonsense. Of course not.
Then I propose the following arrangement for tonight: {NICKNAME}, Odette, and I will form the night watch. We'll sleep in shifts, but two of us must be awake at any given time.

dialogue.sit: Fine by me.
Wait, let me think about this for a second...

dialogue.t: An excellent idea. This allows us to handle the night watch while also keeping an eye on Lelek. Meanwhile, the rule of taking shifts in pairs resolves the other issue — namely, that we can't necessarily trust {NICKNAME} or Valeriy, either.
I expect that plan took you quite some time to come up with, didn't it?
Actually, our Field Combat Manual outlines a similar approach, although the scenario there involves guarding prisoners overnight during field operations.
That being said, I must clarify that I harbor no disrespect towards you personally, Miss Odette.
In fact, Lelek's numerous covert operations make fine textbook examples for military agents.
I care less about respect and more about the fact that you just robbed me of two-thirds of my sleep tonight.
I'm calling dibs on being the first to rest. Goodnight.

dialogue.sit: As night falls, you and Valeriy take the first watch together.
Everyone is sleeping on the stage, making for a scene right out of absurdist theater. Eventually, the time comes for the first shift change...

dialogue.t: It's almost time. We should wake Odette. How are you faring?

dialogue.sit: I'm not sleepy.
You get some sleep. I'll go after you.

dialogue.t: Not going to argue with that. I'll take a quick nap. If you start to feel sleepy, wake me up anytime.

dialogue.sit: (It's finally time for Odette and I to share the night watch. I should wake her up...)
(I came here to get information from her in the first place. Maybe I should think about what questions I want to ask before she wakes up...)

dialogue.t: ...How long are you gonna keep staring at me?

dialogue.sit: You're awake?
But I didn't even wake you yet...

dialogue.t: Couldn't sleep. My mind's been running haywire.
Plus... There's something I've been meaning to talk to you about.

dialogue.sit: You too?

dialogue.t: I had a hunch that you wanted a conversation, too. Let's take this chance to clear the air, shall we?
I just had a simple question for you, really. It's, um...
Rosalyne... In her final moments, did she have any... last words or anything...?

dialogue.sit: Not that I remember.
It all happened so fast.

dialogue.t: Phew... I see. Well, that was all. I have no other questions.

dialogue.sit: Do you miss her?

dialogue.t: No.
She was utterly ruthless in pursuing her goals. That kind of person should be hard to miss.
...And yet... Even though I never approved of her methods, and she was an abrasive person... The fact remains that I am indebted to her.

dialogue.sit: I heard a little about that from Sandrone.

dialogue.t: Oh, she told you... I guess that makes sense. I think she and Rosalyne were on pretty good terms.

dialogue.sit: Still, she didn't know the full details.

dialogue.t: Yes, Rosalyne wasn't the kind to gossip about this sort of thing. Not that it's any huge secret to me, though.
When I was a child, I had to join the Fatui for the sake of my mother and me. I trained under Rosalyne.
It was extremely grueling, and it didn't exactly come naturally to me. All I could do was try to ignore the biting cold and practice, practice, practice.
I was a newcomer who'd managed to make a good first impression on a Harbinger. There was... pressure to live up to her expectations, to be worthy of the Fair Lady's reputation.
Every day was a struggle against the cold, pain, and fatigue... And most nights, I struggled to fall asleep...
After enduring all that, I've become almost immune to the sensation of pain. I suppose that was the cost of survival.
...Surely, any child who had to experience that would grow to hate her lot in life, don't you think?

dialogue.sit: You really paid an enormous price...

dialogue.t: So I put an equal amount of effort into my ballet. Because in my young mind, that was the only way to defy my fate.
It was my way of telling her: "The Fatui's demands and your expectations of me are not what I wish for. One day, I will leave."
I think she probably blamed my poor performance in training on my passion for ballet. She knew my heart wasn't in it.
One time, when I was secretly practicing a dance at night, she suddenly showed up. I knew she was there to catch me red-handed.
I told her, "You don't deserve to watch the dance I learned from my mother."
She looked stunned. I guess she was surprised that I lashed out first, before she had the chance.
But strangely enough, on that occasion, she wasn't fierce with me like she was during training. Instead, she fell silent for a moment and then left.
After that, she never interfered with my dancing or asked me how it was going. She never came to watch me dance again, either. Not even once.

dialogue.sit: She was a very proud person.

dialogue.t: She was. But even now, whenever I take out this Cor Ignis... I can't help but think of that night. Of the look on her face.

dialogue.sit: So this was a gift from her?

dialogue.t: ...Sort of, although "gift" might be too kind a term. This is her flame sealed within ice. A symbol of her favor, yes, but also her way of keeping an eye on people.
She knew the location of every piece of Cor Ignis. If any recipient started acting suspiciously, she'd be onto them immediately. Heh, trust her to make even a mark of approval feel suffocating...
So, when news of Rosalyne's death reached Snezhnaya, many people immediately crushed their Cor Ignis. It gave them a profound sense of relief, like they'd broken free from her shackles.
But I kept mine... With my sensitivity to pain being as dull as it is, the warmth from this Cor Ignis is one of the few things I can still feel clearly.
I still wonder... Did she really come to stop me that night? I wasn't sure, but I was scared, so I said some really awful things.
I guess she didn't leave anything behind... Not that I expected her to. It's fine. It's just a bit of a shame that we couldn't settle our differences before the end.

dialogue.sit: Wait, but...
Sandrone told me you two had settled things...

dialogue.t: Hmm? She did? Are you sure she was talking about this event?

dialogue.sit: She said that Arlecchino gave Rosalyne some advice...
...And that Rosalyne went to see you...

dialogue.t: Huh. No, she didn't. I didn't even find out that she'd gone to Mondstadt until a while after she'd left.
Wait, in that case...

dialogue.sit: I think you should go and see The Knave.

dialogue.t: Okay... I will. Thanks for letting me know.

dialogue.sit: There's something I'm trying to figure out... I'm beginning to suspect that Paimon's mystery illness is being caused by the energy research behind Project Stuzha.
Paimon's very important to me, so I have to get to the bottom of this. I figured that since you're Lelek, you might know something about all this.

dialogue.t: ...The ultimate goal of this energy experiment is to create a weapon for the final battle.
The weapon's construction was completed in Nod-Krai. Now, all that remains is to arm it with a sufficiently powerful energy.

dialogue.sit: So that's what they were doing at the Experimental Design Bureau...
So this is the purpose of the energy experiments...

dialogue.t: Yes. The weapon's development and all the related experiments are overseen by Lord Pierro, "The Jester," and the lab is located deep within the Armory Palace.
I'm not sure why this experiment would be making Paimon feel unwell, though. The best way to get to the bottom of it would be to go there in person.
Once we get out of here, I'll help you apply for an entry permit.

dialogue.sit: Are you sure?
Let's not forget that you're also a Fatuus.

dialogue.t: And I'm hardly the organization's proudest member, as you know. You answered my question about Rosalyne. I want to do you a favor in return. It's that simple.
Ahem... *cough*

dialogue.sit: Hmm? What's wrong? Are you not feeling well?

dialogue.t: *cough*...
You two seem to be hitting it off.

dialogue.sit: Phew, you made me jump!
(Stay calm, just act normal...)

dialogue.t: I thought you were sleeping?
Hah. Of course I was. In the military, one learns to fall asleep quickly, even in the most inhospitable environments. It's vital to staying alert and energized... Why, is something wrong?

dialogue.sit: No no, nothing, nothing...
(Even if he was awake... He can't have overheard us, right?)

dialogue.t: Thank you both for keeping watch. {NICKNAME}, I'll take over for now. It's your turn to get some sleep.

dialogue.sit: Sure.
(This is our second night here... But at least I've found out a little more about Paimon's condition.)
(I hope she's been sleeping well the past couple of days...)
(Hmm... Why do I feel like... I'm being watched?)
(...Seriously? Is this payback for when I stared at her earlier? But I thought she was asleep...)
(*sigh* Never mind. I'd better try and get some sleep myself...)

dialogue.t: Hey, what are you spacing out for? Are you reaching your limit, too?

dialogue.sit: Where are we?
I don't know where this is, and yet it feels strangely familiar...

dialogue.t: How long have we been walking for? Do you remember?
Time's lost all meaning. Ever since... ever since we noticed that... that thing above our heads — what was it called again?
A "Star Key"? Or "Key Star"...? Anyway, the person who named it was swallowed by the "black mist."
Whatever it's called... Ever since we noticed it, we've been walking up and up, hoping that as long as we reach it, we can find a way out of this place.
But it seems like no matter how far we walk, we never get any closer...
*sigh* Well, we've come this far. You never know... Maybe we're almost there? C'mon, enough moping — let's go. The black mist is catching up.
Are you hurt, Kulish?
No, I'm fine. It's just... Suddenly, I don't want to walk any further.
I... I get you... In fact, I reached my limit a long time ago. Sometimes it feels like... like there's hope where there shouldn't be.
Yeah, the hope that that star gives us is the only thing keeping us going. But I'm not sure it's real at all... it may just be a collective illusion.
Otherwise... why would it always be out of reach?

dialogue.sit: Are you really going to give up like this?
I actually feel like we're slowly getting closer to it...

dialogue.t: We know you mean well. But you're only saying that to try and encourage us to keep going, aren't you?
Thank you, friend, but enough is enough. Please don't give me any more false hope. Hope is poison in this place.
You're going to continue, aren't you? I admire that. I've given up, but I wish you the best. May there come a day that you catch up to the star and leave this godforsaken place.
Congratulations! You're the first person to make it here!

dialogue.sit: I actually made it...
But how did she get here...?
The closer I get to this star, the more familiar it looks...

dialogue.t: I'm the Stars' Envoy.
The black mist has stopped rising. Its hunger is satisfied for now, having devoured your two companions.
This is a good opportunity. I'll let you get some rest before we continue.

dialogue.sit: ...Continue?
Aren't we going to leave?

dialogue.t: Hmm? What do you mean, leave? This star represents the starting point. It's the waypoint for the beginning.
Congratulations on reaching the starting point. Once you are ready, we will head out and walk upwards. I will be right by your side the whole way.

dialogue.sit: After everything I went through to get here... this is just the start?

dialogue.t: Huh? What's wrong? Hey, don't give up before the journey's even begun...!

quests.description: The blizzard has forced you to stay the night in Korolevskiy Theater. But as you all awaken, a complication emerges…

quests.title: Winter's Mysterious Silence

dialogue.t: Rampana! Rampana!!!

dialogue.sit: (Is that... Vodyanitsa's voice? What happened...?)

dialogue.t: Kulish! Wake up, please wake up!!!
A "drama about sleeping," which began as a joke the other day, is now playing out on the stage. No one counted on it being a tragedy.
Everyone is gathered around the two "sleepers" in the center of the stage. Without even inspecting the scene, you already know what has happened, as if someone had told you in advance.
The situation is identical to that of the two casualties yesterday. We cannot ascertain the cause of death.
At least there are some elements that we can rule out this time. They slept on the stage with everyone else, so I suppose the surrounding environment can't be a relevant variable...
Rampana... Kulish...
Weren't some of us keeping watch last night? Three of us, in fact. How could you not notice something was wrong?
I'm as confused as you are. Certainly, nothing unusual happened on my watch.
Likewise. And from what I've observed so far, both Miss Odette and {NICKNAME} can be trusted.

dialogue.sit: No incidents during my watch, either.
I have no reason to suspect Valeriy or Odette, either.

dialogue.t: To be honest, I didn't get a wink of sleep last night... I couldn't help but think I was the target, so I just laid there with my eyes closed.
I heard {NICKNAME} and Lelek chatting, but otherwise I don't recall hearing any commotion during the night.
M—Me too... I didn't wanna wake everyone up, so I was concentrating hard, trying not to cough. I hardly slept at all... If anything had happened, I'm sure I would have noticed.
Then, what could possibly be causing this? Once was bad enough... I can't believe it happened again...
I worked closely with Rampana and Kulish for so long. I never imagined that one day, they'd... and on the stage, of all places...
Vodyanitsa...

dialogue.sit: (Four victims in just two days, and we still don't have a single lead...)
(I need to get to the bottom of this as soon as possible — and above all, keep Tonia safe. I'd never be able to look Childe in the eye again otherwise...)

dialogue.t: Still snowing?
Yes, I just checked. Still no sign of anyone outside, either.
So we only have ourselves to rely on?
If you ask me, this killer can clearly strike whenever they please. The night watch was a useless endeavor from the start...
Lelek must be an expert in poisoning! Clearly, she used some poison that can't be detected on the corpse!
Here we go again.
Listen, I was already thinking to myself last night: Was Lelek's reason for revealing her identity the real story? Well, now I have my answer. It most certainly was not!
She's been playing us for fools! You get off on this, don't you? Revealing your identity, only to carry on with your killing spree?
That's a hideous thought. One that only a hideous mind like yours could dream up.
How dare you...!
That's enough. Yesterday, you named Lelek as a suspect because the victims were both wealthy merchants. Lelek might have had a motive then...
But today's victims were just ordinary people, not to mention that they were colleagues of Odette and mine. What reason would she have to murder them? Let me guess, just to scare you?
Who knows? Maybe you don't know her as well as you think!
Hmph. I implore you all to ask yourselves: How many people are there really in this world that have what it takes to kill another person? Not many, I'd wager.
Lelek is well known to be a ruthless operator, and now she has revealed her identity. How could it be any more obvious?
Everything you've said so far is still just conjecture, which doesn't constitute a concrete lead. You need to back up your claims with some evidence.
How can you defend her, Officer? ...What did she say to you while you were on night watch?
Hmph, maybe I shouldn't be so surprised — you military types are always colluding with criminals to target the rich...
...All so you can get your grubby paws on our hard-earned fortunes, then tell us to fall in line! The Fatui, the Druzhna, and the Rokot... Thugs, the lot of you!
D—Don't you dare...!
Sir, but... You were the one who told us not to stop other people from expressing their opinions yesterday.
Four people have already died... Only yesterday, I was chatting with Mr. Kulish, then we woke up in the morning, and he's...
Turning against one another is the last thing we should be doing right now.
*cough*...
L—Little girl...
Even if... Even if Mr. Chugunov is a puffed-up, pig-headed, windbag who doesn't have a clue what he's talking about...
...He's still one of the victims here, isn't he?
Pfft... Ahem, quite.
I had no intention of resorting to violence. But you're right, Miss Tonia. I ought not prevent him from speaking his mind.
In any case, I believe Mr. Chugunov has calmed down a little now. We may resume our discussion...
I don't think there's any need for that. What is there to discuss? Nothing about this situation is normal.
Did you have an idea, Mitya? You're the brainiac here, right? C'mon, clue us in!
I've been mulling something over. All the leads we have so far concern things from outside the theater. Miss Odette's alter ego, the threats Mr. Chugunov received...

But then there's the two double-murder crime scenes themselves, which have given us absolutely nothing to go on whatsoever. That's highly unusual. Even with the most careful killers, there's always some evidence left behind.
So what are you suggesting?
I think this could be a supernatural event. It isn't characteristic of human-on-human homicide at all.
Uh... Correct me if I'm wrong, but aren't you supposed to be a scientist? That doesn't sound like a conclusion someone like you is supposed to make...

Haha... I got into scientific research because of my insatiable curiosity. But if the present situation defies all known scientific explanations, I don't mind shifting my curiosity toward the paranormal instead.
Now that you mention it... I remember when I first came to the theater, I heard rumors about this place being haunted.
Haunted...!?
Yeah, I... think I heard the same thing. But I mean, they're only rumors, right? We've worked here for years. Surely we would've noticed any spooky goings-on by now?

dialogue.sit: (Well, this has taken an unexpected turn... A haunted theater? If Paimon were here, she'd probably be hiding behind me in fear right now.)

dialogue.t: ...Why don't we take this opportunity to look for clues again with a more open mind? Maybe a different perspective will help us see something different.
Very well. Whether it's criminals or ghosts we're looking for, the same rules apply — everyone needs to tread carefully. I'll move the bodies into the same room for now.
Ah, {NICKNAME}. Since you're here — come take a look at this.

Alyosha found it. We're both curious to hear your perspective. It appears to be a... well, an investigation report — and the focus of the investigation was the rumors of haunting we heard about earlier.

dialogue.sit: (An investigation report, huh? Looks quite old... This person's name looks to be of Sumeru origin to me. Was the investigator from Sumeru?)

dialogue.t: The theater manager must've hired an investigator once specifically to look into this issue. But it doesn't look like anyone ever looked at the report.
Presumably, the manager wanted to know if the supposed "haunting" was dangerous, while also being fearful of word getting out in case it affected the theater's business.

Anyway, the bottom line is — the "haunting" is actually real after all. It's caused by an obstruction in the Ley Lines... Is there any chance this is the key to finally making some progress with the murder cases?

dialogue.sit: (Ley Line problems are pretty unexceptional to me by this point. And while it certainly offers an explanation for the "ghosts"...)
(...It's hard to imagine what connection it could have to these two murder cases.)

dialogue.t: Some of the language that appears at the very end of the report caught my eye. "Angel Civilization," "Ley Line Renovation"...
My area of research doesn't touch on any of that, so it's completely outside of my wheelhouse...
...Huh, a piece of paper just fell out from the report. It landed right by your feet.

dialogue.sit: Let's see...
"Death is near."
I just got goosebumps...
It's pretty ominous, no matter how you look at it.

dialogue.t: How unnerving... It was tucked inside the report, so it must be a note left by the author.
"Death is near"... Is that supposed to be what's going on here? With us, in the theater?
But if so, how did the author foresee it? Could he predict the future somehow?
Maybe things are more complicated than we thought.
...No, wait a second... If we take the report and the note at face value, they completely contradict one another.
The report definitively concludes that the hauntings in the theater are harmless and cannot affect the real world. But the note seems to be warning of potential danger...
The question is... What exactly does the note mean by "death"?

dialogue.sit: Is it simply describing our situation?
Is it referring to the victims?
Or could it refer to the perpetrator?

dialogue.t: Hmm... The various ways we could interpret this key word lead in completely different directions. Let's pause our analysis here for now. I think we need more information.
Valeriy, come take a look at this. You too, {NICKNAME}.
Some sort of notebook... What is it for?
It's the on-duty logbook for the theater. Kulish was the main person to use it.
He mostly used it to record any unusual incidents during a show, audience numbers, exit times, and so on...

dialogue.sit: I saw Kulish at the entrance before coming in.
I think he was holding this book at the time.

dialogue.t: Yes, he'd always have this logbook with him when he checked tickets at the entrance.
This should confirm a lot of key details about the recent show. So? Find anything unusual?
Yes... The number of people. I've checked and double-checked, but the numbers just don't match what's recorded in the logbook.
Apparently... we have an extra person among us.
Are we certain that the logbook is accurate? Could someone have sneaked in without buying a ticket, or something?
Unlikely. Kulish took his duties very seriously. I've rarely seen any errors in his work.
Not to mention that this was a dress rehearsal, meaning smaller audience numbers and tighter ticket restrictions than usual. Everything would have been well within his control.
Hmm... We no longer have our tickets with us, do we? They got collected on entry. I assume there's no way we can check them again?
Unfortunately not. The theater recycles tickets. Once people are in the door, they don't tend to leave until the show ends, so we collect the tickets at the point of entry.

dialogue.sit: Too bad Kulish is dead...
If he were still around, we could just ask him.

dialogue.t: Mm. Still... I'm inclined to believe that this discrepancy in the headcount is significant somehow.
Did an extra person just materialize out of thin air...?

dialogue.sit: Tonia? Did you find anything?

dialogue.t: Not yet. Still looking. So, are we, um... are we supposed to be looking for something paranormal...? I—I think I'd prefer teaming up with you than looking around on my own...

dialogue.sit: This looks like... somebody's notebook. Shall we read it together?

dialogue.t: Umm... Well, it doesn't look scary or anything.... so, I guess it should be fine...
...Alright. Let's read it together.

dialogue.sit: (Huh. This has to be Vodyanitsa's writing, surely...)

dialogue.t: Hmm... Maybe it's a little rude for us to peek at this. I feel like I just read someone's secret diary by accident...

dialogue.sit: Since it's an accident, it should be fine...
...Now I feel a little guilty too.

dialogue.t: It sounds like she's writing this for her parents, right? I don't understand — why put this stuff in a notebook instead of mailing it in a letter?
Because her Water Imp parents belonged to the aristocracy, who were driven out of Snezhnaya by the Tsaritsa long ago. And now they live somewhere new, where the postman can't get to.

dialogue.sit: Oh, uh... Hey, Vodyanitsa...
I can explain...

dialogue.t: We're sorry!
It's fine. My fault for not storing it properly. I can't leave things lying around and expect them to get ignored when everyone's scouring the place for clues.
Alright, gimme my notebook back. I'll take over the investigation in this room.
Aaaaaaah! How did I forget about this!? Oh no, not this page... Oh god, and this one... Oh, my... WHY AM I SO EMBARRASSING!?
Aaaaaaaaaaah!
I need to think very hard about whether there's anything that ever needed hiding... After all these years, there must be some things even I've forgotten about...
Chin up, my man. That soldier guy just gave you a bit of a fright, that's all. Think about your wife and kids back home, that'll get you your mojo back.
Me, for example — whenever I get hungry, tired, sleepy, or thirsty, I just think about that Water Imp friend of mine and everything's suddenly alright again.
So daydreaming about women somehow removes your need for food and water, does it? Don't be absurd.
...If we take all this together, it's not impossible, is it? If anything, it's the natural conclusion.

I beg to differ. This sounds to me like the product of a researcher's vivid imagination... Perhaps it's because I'm still viewing this through the lens of a typical murder investigation, but still. I'm struggling to be persuaded by your theory.
*sigh*... Does it really sound that far-fetched? Alright, well, let's treat that as speculation for now. I do agree with what you've said, so let's go with your idea for now.
Good. Okay, now that we finally have some meaningful leads, I think it's time to reconvene. Let's get the others.

dialogue.sit: Everyone gathers back on the stage and shares the information they've found...

dialogue.t: ...So, that's about everything we've discovered so far.
I'll share my theory first. Based on what we've learned from the logbook, I believe the extra person among us is most likely the killer.
If the killer had simply bought a ticket, it would have greatly increased the risk of their identity being exposed.
I expect he or she either hid in the theater ahead of time, or found a way to slip past the ticket inspection. They then blended in with the group and waited for an opportunity to strike.
What about the note found in the investigation report? Any thoughts on how that fits in?
The killer may simply have planted it there as some sort of sick joke. I've seen my fair share of psychopathic killers. They love playing cryptic mind games.
So it has nothing to do with the haunting of the theater after all...
This theory makes sense to me. If we have an audience member unaccounted for, chances are they didn't come here to watch the show.

dialogue.sit: (Could it really be that simple?)

dialogue.t: So in other words, all we have to do is find out who got in here without a ticket, and all our problems will be solved?
Then let me make one thing clear: All the theater staff should be well aware that I came here for the rehearsal legitimately, yes? There's no way I'm the one who didn't have a ticket.
It's true. I hear you used every trick in the book to get a hold of that ticket, too. Everything short of throwing a temper tantrum and rolling around on the floor at the entrance.
I... I most certainly did not degrade myself in such a way!
Probably a stupid question, but I might as well ask... Did anyone here get in without having their ticket checked?
Heh. Guess it was naive of me to expect them to just admit to it...
Especially after the unprompted Lelek reveal. Once was already a miracle, twice would be unfathomable.

dialogue.sit: Mr. Shram... did you really go through the ticket inspection to get in here?

dialogue.t: Huh? Me? Why am I being singled out, my friend? Do I seem that suspicious?
It's not that you stand out as suspicious. More that everyone else has been ruled out as trustworthy.

Okay... Well, we've spent the best part of two days together now, so I'm sure you all can tell what kind of person I am. I'm a true gentleman. I'd never dream of doing something like sneaking into the theater without a ticket.
Yeah, I have no doubt that you're a good person. But the problem is... none of us here actually know you, so no one can say for sure that you are who you claim to be...
Although actually... What was it you said last night...? Yeah, you're friends with that Water Imp, which is why you understand our primary mode of expression.

Last time I checked, there were barely any of us remaining in Snezhnaya, since most of the Water Imps left. Could you tell me a little bit more about your friend? There's a good chance I actually know her.
...And I suppose it's also kind of a way for everyone else to get to know you a little better.
Ah... I, uh... hahahaha... umm...
Good grief... Are you blushing? Pull yourself together, man. Stop giggling like a teenage boy, it's revolting...
Hey, "revolting" is a little strong! ...Alright, fine, I'll admit it. That Water Imp "friend" of mine... the truth is, we're dating.

I was just a bodyguard hired by her family, but the stars must have aligned, because sparks began to fly between me and their daughter... Hahaha, never in my wildest dreams did I think I'd get so lucky.
We don't need details. Just get to the point.
Okay, okay. I'm just a little hesitant to reveal her name, that's all... You know how it is. These are delicate times...
Even with me to protect her... If word gets out that she's dating a human, both the fae and human factions will give her a hard time.
Really? Wait, no... That can't be...
Huh? Shram... What the devil are you talking about?
Hmm? Why is everyone looking at me like that? Surely you can understand where I'm coming from...?
"Delicate times"...? "Factions"...?
Uh... Yes? You know, the civil war? Last time I checked, the fae and the humans were still at each other's throats...
If I'm not mistaken... the last significant civil war in Snezhnayan history was over four hundred years ago, when Her Majesty the Tsaritsa had just taken the throne and was consolidating her reign.
...Wh—What do you mean, four hundred years ago?

dialogue.sit: (What's going on here? Is Shram from the past?)

dialogue.t: Alright, Mr. Mitya, you win this round. As far-fetched as it is... it appears that your theory may be correct.
I'm just as amazed as you are... I didn't even believe it myself, to be honest.
Is someone going to explain what's going on here?
From the look on your face, you've figured it out too, haven't you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: Three logic puzzles

dialogue.t: Yeah, the logic is clear now. The investigation report said that there would be souls stuck wandering the theater because the Ley Lines here are cut off.
Mr. Shram must be one such soul, who died in the theater a long time ago. In which case... that also makes him our extra person.
So when that note said "death is near," it must have been referring to "death" as in the deceased. People who died a long time ago.
Someone who died a long time ago...
In short, there's a dead person among us. The extra person we've been searching for is a ghost from the past.
You mean I'm a ghost? No, no, no... Don't make jokes like that, my man. There must be some mistake.
But even if I was dead, I know for a fact I didn't kill anyone these past two nights!
Yeah. Even if all that's true, the report also said the souls inside the theater can't affect reality, right? They're harmless.
Hmm... Then, what if the problem isn't the souls at all... but the Ley Lines themselves?

The Ley Lines have a powerful ability to attract and devour souls. Let's say that the Ley Lines are like a "black hole," constantly seeking to engulf souls, but the souls that don't want to return are trying to avoid being sucked in...

dialogue.sit: (Huh... Why does this analogy sound so familiar?)

dialogue.t: What happens when the "black hole" can't achieve its goal? I'm only speculating here but, but... what if it ended up swallowing innocent souls by mistake? Or intentionally taking other souls to compensate?
That could explain why we weren't able to determine a cause of death. If you're right, and their souls were devoured by the Ley Lines... it does make some sense.
It does seem to explain a lot of the things we couldn't make sense of... Does that mean it's true?

dialogue.sit: (Except there's no concrete evidence. Mitya is relying on a lot of logical leaps...)
(Still, it seems like the best explanation we have under the circumstances...)

dialogue.t: Alright, so how could Shram not know that he's dead? Seems a little unlikely that he hasn't noticed anything unusual even after several days interacting with us.
On the contrary, it's perfectly normal for a soul to wander the theater for centuries without questioning their existence or reason for being there. It's simply what's natural for them.
Uh... Um... Huh.
You know what, Mr. Brainiac? I think you might actually be right after all...
I'm trying to remember, and... Ugh... Even though my head feels like it's going to explode, I think... it's all coming back to me...
...I was the one who didn't want to remember my own death. So I forced myself to forget.
Well... I'm sure those are painful memories.
My lady and I snuck out to go on a date one day. We bought tickets for the theater. It wasn't really my thing, but I was just happy to be together.
All of a sudden, a group of people burst into the theater, shouting for all the Water Imps to get out... performers and audience members included.
It was clear the conflict between humans and fae had reached a boiling point. This time, the extremists were even coming after the Water Imps who had nothing to do with the war.
I thought I could pull one over on them, so I took off my jacket, draped it over my lady, and tried to sneak out amid the chaos...
But I got caught. They started shouting, calling me a... a traitor to humanity.
But I was going to do whatever it took to buy her a chance to escape, no matter how many people stood in my way. I had to, both as her bodyguard... and out of love.
It's alright, friend. You can stop there if you want. You don't need to dig all that up again.
It's just... *sigh*... Even now, I'm still struggling to accept the truth. How could I... be dead?
I'm... sorry, everyone.
If I'd known I was a dead man walking, I wouldn't have dragged you down with me, haha. If I'm the cause of all this death, then punish me however you see fit.
But Mr. Shram...
No, I refuse to be a burden. I know what I have to do. You said I've been wandering the theater for centuries, right?
I guess it's high time I got a breath of fresh air... Out there, I mean. I'll leave this place, and take all this "death" with me. Go out on my own terms.
Mr. Shram, I'm sure we can figure out a different course of action...

My good sir, we both know I'm not supposed to be here. I should have accepted my death long ago... One way or another, this has to end. Unless you're saying this goes against another one of your military principles somehow?
No, I'm speaking on a personal level this time.
Let it go, man. ...Oh, wait, one last thing. Miss Water Imp, my... my lover — her name was Litiya. Litiya Ozerova. Do you know what happened to her?
Ozerova... Oh, Auntie Ozerova! That's what we all called her. I remember her as a very kind elder! She had a bunch of kids too!
Hahaha... Ah, I'm so glad she survived. And she had lots of kids? Good. That's... good. I could hardly expect her to stay single just because of what happened to me, right? Haha...

As long as she went on to be happy, that's all that matters. *sigh* Besides, I'm dead. My soul has been wandering around here for so long because I was worried about her. But now... I can go without regret.
There's no need to see me off, my friends. I've enjoyed our time together over these past few days. Perhaps... we'll meet again in the next life.
Take care... my man.
I know Mr. Shram was already dead, but... I still feel so sad.
Death is cruel, no matter how we might try to make sense of it...

So, was the conflict between fae and humans really that bad back then? I was only little, so I don't remember much. It's terrible to think that so many innocent people had their lives turned upside down...
Even the historical records about that time period don't say much about it.
All people know is that the Tsaritsa founded the Fatui, drove out most of the fae aristocracy without explanation, then used her terrifying power to suppress the humans.
It seems to me like the Tsaritsa chose to make herself the enemy. She downplayed the conflict, directing whatever animosity both sides had for each other at herself instead.
That's also why, despite how brutal the conflict was at the time, there hasn't been much lingering tension between humans and fae since. Things have been fairly harmonious for the past few centuries.
So, the Tsaritsa banished the fae... to protect the fae living in the city? She offered herself up to be hated in exchange for peace...
Maybe it's not quite as bad as it sounds. I don't think Her Majesty is too concerned if mortals hate her or not, and besides, there are very few who truly do.
All this time, I had no idea...
Alright, if Mitya's theory is correct, then I think we can consider this matter settled. Let's all take a break.
*sigh* If only this blasted storm wasn't still raging on...

dialogue.sit: (Looks like now we can just rest until the snowstorm stops...)
(I still can't believe Shram turned out to be a ghost who'd been in the theater for hundreds of years. To think he was dead this whole time... What a strange turn of events.)

dialogue.t: Knock, knock.
Knock, knock.

dialogue.sit: Uh... You know the door isn't closed, right? You don't have to knock.

dialogue.t: Think of it as a signal then. When I'm entering someone else's room and I knock, I'm here as Odette. If I don't knock, it's Lelek.

dialogue.sit: Sure, whatever makes you happy.
Please come in, Miss Odette.

dialogue.t: Thanks.

dialogue.sit: So, why did you come to find me? Is there something I can help with?

dialogue.t: Vodyanitsa said you knew about my secret identity from the start.
But when everyone was discussing who Lelek could be, you were worried that revealing what you knew would be unfair to me, so you kept it to yourself, right?

dialogue.sit: ...That's what you wanted to talk about?
You just came here to thank me?

dialogue.t: Yes, I'm extremely grateful for that.

dialogue.sit: It's nothing. I mean, you didn't hold what happened with Signora against me, so... I should thank you for that as well.

dialogue.t: Actually, there's something else as well... I've found myself in a situation similar to the one you were in when you helped conceal my identity.
So I thought I'd come and ask you for advice.

dialogue.sit: I'm honored.
What's the situation?

dialogue.t: It's about Mitya...
Before all of this, the last time I saw him... He was dead.

dialogue.sit: What!?

dialogue.t: As I'm sure you know, my goal as Lelek was to stop Project Stuzha.
Well, when I found out the tech lead for the experiment behind Project Stuzha was Mitya, I immediately started planning to track him down and threaten him to back out.
I often saw him around the theater, but I soon concluded that making my move there would risk exposing my identity...
So I decided to infiltrate the Armory Palace and go directly to his lab. That way, the threat would be much more effective.

dialogue.sit: That must be basically the most classified place in Snezhnaya...
If you managed to infiltrate it... You really do have what it takes to be a Harbinger.

dialogue.t: Well... I suppose there was a bit of luck involved. But I am a Fatuus, so I already had some familiarity with the building's layout.
But when I finally made it to his lab, Mitya seemed to be... dead.

dialogue.sit: How did you know?
Are you sure he wasn't just dozing off?

dialogue.t: I checked his breathing and his pulse. He had no vital signs whatsoever. I'm certain of that.
I thought maybe another anti-Project Stuzha activist had beaten me to it, and chosen a much more brutal method... so I made myself scarce.

dialogue.sit: That's why you were so on guard around Mitya that first night here.

dialogue.t: Yes, when I saw him sitting in the audience during the performance, I could barely contain the shock...
