To me, it was a miracle. Somehow, he'd come back from the dead... But then, the murders started happening and things got so complicated that it wasn't really at the front of my mind.
That is, until Mitya himself said there must be a dead person among us... Then, I couldn't ignore it any longer.

dialogue.sit: And yet... You thought that bringing it up right away would single Mitya out, just like when everyone was suspecting Lelek.

dialogue.t: Exactly. I thought there could be something I was missing...
Besides, we soon figured out that Mr. Shram was a ghost, and we knew there was only one extra person, so we thought he had to be the one.

dialogue.sit: But now, it seems like there's another candidate...
I understand why you kept it to yourself. There was so much information being thrown around during that discussion, bringing up Mitya would have just introduced more confusion.

dialogue.t: So, what do you think we should do?

dialogue.sit: Let me confirm one thing first. When was it that you found Mitya dead?

dialogue.t: Around a week ago. Sometime in the afternoon.

dialogue.sit: A week ago... That's earlier than I thought. I saw him just a few days ago at a restaurant. That definitely would have been after you found him dead.
He seemed completely normal to me. Chatting with Vodyanitsa, trying to avoid Valeriy...

dialogue.t: So he was definitely alive on that day. Huh... Well, all I can say is, I know what I saw.

dialogue.sit: Here's a thought. The reason we even suspected a dead person could be among us was because of the problem with the theater's Ley Lines...
But Mitya's death happened inside the Armory Palace. The Ley Lines affecting the theater shouldn't reach that far.

dialogue.t: You're right. I guess he doesn't fit the profile of the person we were searching for.

dialogue.sit: I think the chances of it being him are very low. Surely he can't have died for real in the Armory Palace... Unless...

dialogue.t: Unless what?

dialogue.sit: Unless he really did come back from the dead.

dialogue.t: ...Hmm, you're right. Do you think we need to disclose this to the others?
Huh? What's this? A private meet-and-greet?
Where do I line up?
...That's not what's going on here.
Haha... Well, I was just making the rounds. Thought I'd try to lighten the mood a bit. Vodyanitsa's handing out food if you're hungry.
I was actually planning on hiring him as my bodyguard after we got out of here, you know... *sigh* Poor guy.
Even though Shram was already deceased, his decision to walk into the snowstorm was still a sacrifice, and a very brave one.
This is one of the few times I don't feel at all happy to have my theory proven true.
Well, at least it seems like Mr. Shram stayed optimistic until the end.
The information he revealed... it's given me a lot to think about.
At least the lingering regret that kept him here has been put to rest. That's not necessarily a bad thing.

dialogue.sit: Outside, the snowstorm continues to rage, and before you know it, night falls once more.

dialogue.t: What is going on with this storm? Could it be connected to that monster that just arrived in Snezhnaya?
I almost hope it is. Her Majesty the Tsaritsa left to vanquish that beast herself. We just need to wait for her triumphant return.
Do you think... people still feel the cold after they die? I'm wondering about Shram... Maybe we should have given him a coat before he went out there.
Death itself is cold, isn't it? I'm sure the storm will embrace him.
Well, I hope he has a safe journey. I'm going to miss him, I think... It's not like we can blame him for Rampana and Kulish's deaths.
Thinking back on it, we barely made it out alive ourselves...
Once we get out of here, how are we going to explain what happened to their families...?
*cough*... *cough*...
...Are you okay? Here, take this. I've never used it.
*cough*... Thanks...
Look who's Mr. Nice Guy all of a sudden. Is it because Tonia stood up for you this morning? At least you know how to return a favor.
Yeah, without Tonia, who knows how badly he would have been hurt.
*sigh*... I told you already, I never intended to resort to violence.
...Bunch of rascals.
Um... Little girl, I was rather surprised when you spoke up for me this morning. I didn't think I had many admirers here, so, um... Thank you.
Oh... No need to thank me. I said some bad stuff about you too...
I've been too embarrassed to admit it, but, uh... You remind me a lot of my daughter.
So kind to everyone, but never lets her old man off the hook... Unless my wife and I are having a fight. Then, she's always on my side...
Especially when she was little. Every time I took her out—
*cough*... *cough*...
Alright, easy now... How long have you had that cough, Tonia?
*cough*... I don't know. It's probably been a while... *cough* I'm fine.
Are you taking anything for it?
Yeah. I'll be fine once I see my brother. He's gonna pick some Frostfairy Flower leaves and brew a tonic for me. I'll feel much better once I drink that.
I see. That's good to hear, then.
We should probably discuss arrangements for tonight. Now that the deceased has left our midst, there shouldn't be any more incidents.
However, out of an abundance of caution, I'll keep watch.
Shouldn't we take shifts? I can take one if needed.
No need. I managed to get a nap in earlier, so I have plenty of energy right now. After all the tension of the past few days, everyone else should just focus on getting a good night's sleep.

dialogue.sit: (What a long day... This whole situation turned out to be way more complicated than I expected...)
(But Valeriy's right. I should just try to calm down and get some rest... The last thing I want is to give myself nightmares.)

dialogue.t: He(She)'s awake... He(She)'s awake! Get over here you big lug, and take a look!
If you must call me something, call me Mr. Door. The black mist is coming. You need to go.

dialogue.sit: Where are we?
"Black mist"... Haven't I heard that before...?

dialogue.t: Are you alright? Can you walk? We just got attacked by monsters on our way up. That Mr. Door fellow protected us.
He just seemed to come out of nowhere. Not much of a talker, but when it comes to taking down monsters, that man doesn't hold back...
Curses. The black mist is catching up to us. We need to keep going.
I'm so exhausted... and the black mist is still rising... *sigh*...
Wait, look! There's more monsters down there! Are they coming from within the black mist?
No, no! They're gaining on us! Quick, keep going, or they'll be at our heels any second!
Mr. Door! What are you doing!? We need to get out of here, they're coming!
Found it.
This is my "door."
Wh—What? You mean, you're going to stay here?
I am a door. This is where my duty lies.

dialogue.sit: So he meant a door for closing, not for opening...

dialogue.t: No! You saved us. We can't leave you behind!
You must keep going. A door can only keep things out for so long. You must make haste.
But...
...You're right. Let's go! We can't let Mr. Door's sacrifice be in vain!
The black mist isn't moving anymore. Looks like both the monsters and Mr. Door are gone.
I... I didn't just imagine all that, did I?
Surely, I wasn't so scared out of my mind that I hallucinated a door as a human being?

dialogue.sit: No. I remember Mr. Door too.

dialogue.t: Okay, good... There's no way we both hallucinated the same thing.
...Hmm? Getting sleepy? Well, looks like we're safe for now. Go ahead. Let's get some rest...

quests.description: Successive deaths occur within the theater, but there seems to be no clues as to the perpetrator. You gradually realize that this may not be some ordinary occurrence…

quests.title: Wraith's Nocturne

dialogue.sit: (...What time is it? Is it morning? I think I had a nightmare...)
(I guess everyone's still asleep? These past two days have been exhausting. Valeriy's keeping watch, though, so he's probably the only one awake...)
(Valeriy...?)

dialogue.t: Just like the last two nights... No clear cause of death.
I've been a real thorn in your side, haven't I, Mr. Valeriy. Now you can rest in peace.
But for me... Life will be all the duller for not having to run away from you, my friend.
How's Tonia? Is she okay?
I just checked on her, and it doesn't seem like anything serious. She's just exhausted from the past couple of days, and she's still recovering from her illness. We should let her sleep a bit longer.
That means Valeriy was the only one who died last night.
If Valeriy was awake and keeping watch, it would have been impossible to kill him without waking everyone else up. That much is certain.
This is so frustrating! Why has nothing changed since yesterday? I thought we already dealt with the dead person causing all this!
Actually, one thing has changed. There's only one victim this time, not two. Does that mean...

dialogue.sit: The number of people who die each night is equivalent to the number of dead among us. That's your theory, right?

dialogue.t: Exactly. We identified Mr. Shram, and the night after he left, the death toll dropped from two to one.
By that logic... there must be one more dead person left among us.
Another one? But there was only one person unaccounted for in the ticket checks, right? The head count should match up now...
Having an extra person was definitely a cause for alarm, but being one person short isn't nearly as unusual. Someone could have left in the middle of the show, or made it out before the storm hit...

dialogue.sit: (One more dead person among us... If Mitya's theory is right, then what Odette told me seems a lot more relevant...)
(It's just, at the time, we had no reason to think there was more than one dead person.)
(*sigh*... If only we'd taken it more seriously as a possibility... Maybe this could have been avoided...)

dialogue.t: I'm sorry, this is my fault. I had information that could have been helpful, but I held back. I should have brought it up right away.

dialogue.sit: I'm partly to blame as well. I was too quick to dismiss Odette's concerns...

dialogue.t: What is this about? ...What have you two been getting up to behind my back?
Sounds like there's some big news you've been keeping from the rest of us. Well, we're all ears.

dialogue.sit: Odette tells the group about finding Mitya dead, and your discussion yesterday.

dialogue.t: I... I'm the dead person...?
Uh, wow... That's certainly news to me...

dialogue.sit: Odette and I talked about it yesterday, but we thought it just wasn't possible, so we left it at that.

dialogue.t: Yeah, I don't blame you. If I'd been there, I probably would have reached the same conclusion... It just sounds too unbelievable.
Let me just try and verify this. I just scoured my memories, trying to think back to the afternoon Miss Odette mentioned...
But I honestly have no recollection of dying. That's where I'm different than Mr. Shram.
Hmm... Having seen Mr. Mitya a few days ago myself, I also find it hard to believe he could be the other dead person among us.
Well, if it isn't Mitya, then who? Do we vote on it?
If you don't mind me asking, {NICKNAME}... I believe you mentioned that you know Tonia's brother? Had you ever met her before all this?

dialogue.sit: No, never. Wait, are you saying...

dialogue.t: Now just one minute! I know where this is going. You can't just randomly point a finger at anyone you want...
You're in the hot seat, and all of a sudden you want to divert our suspicions onto somebody else?
Trying to pick a fight, Mr. Chugunov? Whenever you open your mouth, all you do is attack people, and I've had enough of it. If you don't want to engage in a civil discussion, you can shut up.
You... little... brat!

dialogue.sit: (Did Mitya ask about Tonia because he suspects her?)
(I suppose I only identified her by her age, and nothing else. Could that mean...)

dialogue.t: I—I'm just saying, you're going around casting suspicion on people for no reason. How could Tonia be dead?
I can vouch for her, if nothing else. I've seen her before. She's the sister of that... that Harbinger, isn't she? The one called "Childe."
Oh, really? You're telling the truth?

dialogue.sit: (Since being here, I don't think I ever mentioned she was Childe's sister specifically... Does Chugunov actually know her?)

dialogue.t: If Chugunov can vouch for her, then it can't be Tonia either. In which case, it seems unlikely that there's another dead person among us at all...
Miss Odette, could you go over that afternoon with me one more time? When you found me "dead"...
No problem.
Huh... No matter how hard I try, I just can't remember anything about dying. But I do remember something else...
Miss Vodyanitsa, during our last meal together, I told you how some of the researchers were suffering from temporary memory loss. Do you remember that?
Oh, yeah. You said it was hindering the progress of your experiments? You thought they were just under too much stress or something.
Right. And even though I don't remember "dying" that day, I'm pretty sure I experienced something like amnesia...
Some of my memories from that afternoon... are missing.
Are you suggesting you're missing the memory of your...
Of course, how am I only just realizing this... Humans aren't necessarily aware of their own death.
You mean, being silently assassinated? Or dying in your sleep? Situations like that?
The researchers' amnesia... suddenly it all makes sense...
I must thank you, Odette. I think your perspective just helped me reach a breakthrough on a series of issues that have been troubling me for quite some time.
Alright, it's decided then. I'll be the one to leave today.
Leave? Hey, hey, wait a minute, aren't you rushing into this? What if you're wrong? You'll pay with your life!
Come on, kid... Aren't you going to fight for your life? This seems like a rash decision...
I have other reasons, beyond what's been discussed. In fact... thinking back...
I remember during Miss Odette's performance, while I was sitting in the audience stalls, a brilliant new idea for my research popped into my mind. But then, my train of thought suddenly cut off.
I can't remember it now at all, and I didn't take any notes... I guess that must be another instance of temporary amnesia.
No, no, hold on, I see where you're going with this. You're suggesting that each instance of temporary amnesia is a death, right?
There's a glaringly obvious flaw in that idea, no? How can one person die so many times?
I believe Miss Odette's account. During the period where my memory is blank, I must have been either dead or in a similar state.

All it would take is for the same thing to happen in the theater, and I would come under the effect of the Ley Lines in this vicinity. This increases the likelihood of me being the deceased, does it not?
I... But...
There's no evidence to suggest that anyone other than me is a candidate for the deceased. So allow me, as a scientist, to treat this as an experiment.
Please relax, everyone. I don't think things are as bad as they may seem. If I really am the deceased, then to leave the theater will be a relief for me.
If, on the other hand, I'm still alive right now — well, apparently you've all witnessed my resurrection recently anyway. Who's to say I won't return from the dead again this time?

dialogue.sit: (Mitya's right. This is the only thing we can try right now... I think he's deliberately downplaying the gravity of the situation, though. He probably doesn't want to burden everyone.)

dialogue.t: What is a scientist, if not someone who gambles on experiment after experiment in an attempt to obtain the truth?
With this snowstorm, the ley line phenomenon, ghosts of the dead, and my "amnesia," we've been paralyzed by not knowing, and powerless to do anything about it. It's a terrible feeling.
But if I do get resurrected, you can be sure that I'll come back with the truth of all this. Just you wait.

dialogue.sit: As night falls, the theater is filled with a heavy silence. More than half of the group is gone since the first night here...

dialogue.t: That Valeriy guy was packing even more muscle than I thought. I can't believe how heavy he was... Hauling him over there nearly killed me.
Curse this confounded snowstorm! Go bother some other poor souls instead!
...What do you want? I'm not in the mood to talk right now.
What's on your mind, Odette? You haven't said a word.
I was thinking about Mitya. If he'd been unwilling to sacrifice himself by walking out into the snowstorm... That would have made more sense to me.
After all, it seems like the dead don't perceive things any differently from the living. Mitya doesn't even remember dying.
So, to hear the news that you're apparently dead, and simply choose to walk out that door without a second thought... I can't imagine all the things that must have been going through his head.
But when Mitya left, his expression revealed absolutely nothing. Perhaps he is even better at disguising himself than I am.
Poor Mr. Mitya... I didn't even get to see him one last time...
Maybe it's a good thing that you weren't there to see it. It was a hard thing to watch.
I hate goodbyes. Why does it feel like everyone around me is slowly disappearing? Not just in here, I mean. In the outside world, too...
Maybe it's the realization that, at the end of life, everyone has to face it alone.
Come to think of it... The main reason we're still alive right now is pure luck. Each morning here, for every one of us, there's the chance that we might not wake up.
You could take it a step further and say that the same is true outside, too... Who can ever be 100% sure when they drift off to sleep that they'll open their eyes again in the morning?
If I make it out of here, I'm going to cherish every moment that I'm awake... and live without any regrets.

dialogue.sit: (Without regrets... hmm...)
(I feel like a strange sense of anxiety has been quietly growing inside me over the last two days...)

dialogue.t: Are you okay? You look really glum...
If something's bugging you, let's talk about it. There's only a few of us left here now. After everything we've been though, what's the point in keeping things bottled up?

dialogue.sit: I have a travel companion named Paimon. Alyosha and Odette have met her before. She's been feeling unwell recently.

dialogue.t: You're worried about her, aren't you? That makes sense. We've been trapped in here for days.

dialogue.sit: To be honest, I used to feel like I was just a spectator in this world, watching everything that happens from the sidelines. Maybe it's because I'm a "Descender."

dialogue.t: ...A "Descender"?

dialogue.sit: But with Paimon by my side, over time, I slowly felt my connection to this world growing stronger.
She loves eating, sleeping, and having fun, but she's also a great guide. It's her authenticity that makes this whole world feel more real for me.
Over the last few days that we've been apart, I've often caught myself wondering... What would Paimon say if she were here right now?
But by the time I snap out of it, the conversation has already moved on, and I'm still in my own little world.
I'm trying to overcome this sense of detachment, but... I really miss Paimon. I guess, in a way... she means the whole world to me.

dialogue.t: I bet she misses you when you're not there as well. Maybe you're her entire world, too.
I don't know if this will make you feel any better, but back when the Water Imps left Snezhnograd in droves, I also felt like the whole world was suddenly empty.
I could be surrounded by people all smiling and having fun, and still feel completely separate from it. So I totally understand how you feel.
Later on I started to think... maybe accepting the fact that our loved ones won't always be with us... is something that takes a lifetime.
All we can do is cherish their companionship from moment to moment.
So, once we get out of here, you better hurry back to her side as fast as you can! You can't let your story end in regret — that's the trope I hate the most!

dialogue.sit: Thank you. That's exactly what I needed to hear.

dialogue.t: But, Vodyanitsa... If you hate goodbyes too, why didn't you leave with your people?
That's just the choice I made. I used to regret it, but I don't anymore.
Like I said before, singing is a Water Imp's primary mode of expression. It's how we convey our emotions.
Our songs have echoed through this theater for hundreds of years, each one a story pieced together through moments of joy and sorrow.
But does a story exist without someone to read it? To me, the answer is no.
So I made the choice to stay. That way, there would still be someone left to sing these songs, and listen to their stories. Otherwise, they could have been lost forever.
Could you teach me how to understand your people's songs sometime? I wanna be able to truly hear them, like Mr. Shram.
Hahaha... A fan after my own heart! Thank you, Tonia. How about I sing something for you, and you tell me what you hear?
Okay! I'll do my best!
I've never heard that one before... I feel like I can hear a sense of... longing somehow. I wonder why that is...
Color me impressed, Tonia! You're a keen listener!
Most people can only tell if a song is happy or sad... I didn't think you'd be able to pick up on such specific details.
Hehe... So, what's the song about then? C'mon, tell me!
I've actually never performed this song in the theater before, because it has more of a ceremonial purpose for our people. It's not meant for the stage.
It means something like... "May those we have lost watch over us and follow this song back home in the night, so that we might be reunited once more."

dialogue.sit: So it's kind of like a requiem?
A call to be reunited with our loved ones in our dreams.

dialogue.t: No wonder I could hear that sense of longing. You sing it for loved ones who have passed away... I hope it reaches them.
It's getting late, Tonia, and you're not well. We should all turn in early. I suppose... there's no reason to keep watch tonight.
Okay. But, um, before I go to bed... Could you sing that song a couple more times for me, Vodyanitsa?
Of course! Anything for my number one fan!

dialogue.sit: (Once I get out of here, I definitely don't plan on ever coming back.)
(But I guess that means I'll never get to hear Vodyanitsa sing again... That's a sad thought.)
(Before I fall asleep, I should cherish this moment of companionship while it lasts.)
(Where... am I?)
(It's so dark in here, and I feel kind of dizzy... Am I alone?)
(Huh? What was that noise...!?)

dialogue.t: Return, O spirits, fulfill your oath of protection...

dialogue.sit: *cough*... *panting*...
I—I'm alive? What just happened...

dialogue.t: No time for questions! Quick, over here. Turn on the switch. We need to bring back the light!
Alright, we're safe. That spirit just now is called "Night Prayer." The light subdues her, but she'll attack without a second thought in the dark.

dialogue.sit: Is... Is she a ghost?

dialogue.t: Umm, sort of. I know it's hard, but you can't let this place go dark, or she'll kill you again.

dialogue.sit: Did I really just die?
She really just killed me?

dialogue.t: Yup. Luckily, I was here to resurrect you, otherwise that'd have been a real bummer.

dialogue.sit: A bit more than a bummer, I'd say... Wait so, you have the ability to resurrect people?

dialogue.t: Sure I do! I'm your guardian spirit, after all.
I specialize in "soul recall." Oh, it's nice to meet you, by the way.

dialogue.sit: Thanks... It's nice to meet you too.

dialogue.t: Alright, there's no time to waste. The black mist is already catching up. We need to avoid it and Night Prayer at all costs. C'mon, let's go.
It's too dark. We're not gonna make it! C'mon, faster!
{NICKNAME}!
I won't let you die like this. Not on my watch!

dialogue.sit: *panting*...
Even though it's not permanent...
Dying is definitely not a pleasant experience.

dialogue.t: Great, you're back.

dialogue.sit: Yeah, thanks to you.

dialogue.t: Time for you to get out of here. Quick, before the light runs out.

dialogue.sit: What about you? You're not coming with me?

dialogue.t: I can't. I've already been "used up".

dialogue.sit: "Used up"?
What does that mean?

dialogue.t: A guardian spirit's skills are finite. I can only resurrect someone so many times.
I might not look any different, but my essence has been exhausted. Now, I will slowly start to fade away.
I can go no further. The black mist is where I belong. It's okay.

dialogue.sit: Why didn't you tell me sooner?

dialogue.t: Because it wouldn't have changed anything. That knowledge would have just burdened you... And a guardian spirit's role is to protect.

dialogue.sit: But...

dialogue.t: Go. Now, before it's too late. I already hear Night Prayer approaching.
*sobbing*... Vodyanitsa! How could this happen? Vodyanitsa!
Well, I guess there's no need to inspect the body.
You're beginning to grow numb to the tragic deaths that await each morning...
Before long, the lament of countless Water Imps seems to resound around the theater, full of deep affection and sorrow for Vodyanitsa.
Your emotions begin to respond in kind, leaving a heavy feeling in your chest.
This wasn't supposed to happen... You lied to us, didn't you, Chugunov? You've been lying from the start...
Take a long, hard look at yourself before you go around accusing other people!
I suspected you on day one, Lelek, and now look where we are! By some strange coincidence, you've never been targeted? You just happen to have survived this long? No, you should be the prime suspect!
And you, little hunter. Ever so content with staying on the sidelines. Yet, you were the one who stopped us from leaving from the start! Why are you trying to keep us here?
Now, you're just lashing out indiscriminately. That's either a sign of anxiety or a guilty conscience.
Where was all this passion and bravado before? Decided to fight until the bitter end, is that it?
Is that a threat? Fine, bring it on! You think I'm afraid to die after all this? You want to kill me? Go ahead. I'd like to see you try!

dialogue.sit: (After all the trauma of the past few days, everyone's been pushed to the breaking point...)
(Valeriy and Mitya aren't here anymore. Someone else needs to step up and take charge...)
(But first, I need to think this through. Considering everyone left, who's the most likely candidate for the "deceased"?)
Identify Tonia
Tonia, how's Teucer been lately?

dialogue.t: ...Teucer?

dialogue.sit: Your brother, Ajax, must have mentioned me in his letters home, right? Did he say anything about a "blond(blonde) Traveler"?

dialogue.t: N—No... And my brother's name is Razyk, not Ajax.
Tch...

dialogue.sit: Chugunov, looks like it's your turn to do some explaining... Yesterday, you said you could vouch for Tonia. Why did you give us a false testimony?

dialogue.t: I knew you were behind this, Chugunov. You've been lying through your teeth from the start.
Everything about you is fake, down to the wife and daughter you're always talking about. Your entire "family man" persona is a charade, isn't it?
That night, when I infiltrated your place as Lelek, I noticed you were home alone. Didn't think much of it at the time — just thought everyone else was out...
But thinking back on it now, that doesn't seem very likely. My guess is... You live alone, don't you?

dialogue.sit: (Even that was a lie? But why would he lie about having a family?)

dialogue.t: Curses... Gah, why is there no end to this blasted snowstorm!? If it would just stop... If it would just stop...
I... I think I remember now. I know how I ended up here. It feels like a distant memory... but at the same time, it's like it was just yesterday...
The reason I'm always coughing is because I got sick with Frostblight. The locals usually call it the snow cough.

It's not a very common illness. It's partly genetic and partly caused by the cold climate, but it can be fatal. They sent me to the hospital as soon as they found out I had it, and I spent so, so long lying there in that hospital bed...

After a while, I felt myself growing weaker and weaker. Nothing seemed to be working anymore — neither the treatment that the doctors were giving me, nor the medicine my brother was brewing from Frostfairy Flower leaves.
So one day, I told my brother that I wanted him to take me outside for once, so things could be like they used to just for one day. I wanted to meet loads of friends, experience new things...
He agreed. He snuck me out of the hospital, and we escaped.
We got to the theater, bought tickets, and went inside. Oh, it was all so exciting... I remember the show very clearly — it was amazing. But I found myself getting sleepier and sleepier...
Oh, Tonia...
When I woke up, I couldn't find my brother anywhere, so I guessed he'd already left.

But there's no way he'd leave me behind. So I decided to stay here and wait for him... At the time, I figured he'd probably gone to brew some more medicine for me. I was planning to chew him out for abandoning me when he got back...
Tonia... It sounds like by then, you'd... already...
Yeah, I know. I understand now — I'm... dead, aren't I? This cough, and the feeling weak, it's probably just my body's memory.
After all that, it turns out I can't blame my brother after all. I was the one who abandoned him...
I'm sorry, everyone. I've realized this much too late. It seems like death skewed my perception... and now I've dragged you all into this mess.

dialogue.sit: Your name probably isn't even "Tonia," is it? Didn't that ever strike you as odd over the last few days?

dialogue.t: Well, when I was little, my brother and I read a storybook, and Tonia is the name of one of the characters.
When we escaped from the hospital, our family and the hospital security were looking everywhere for us.
So when you first approached me and said my brother had sent you, and called me "Tonia"...
I thought he must have chosen a fake name that only the two of us would know, because he was afraid of getting caught... Now, it seems like that was just wishful thinking.
At least your memory of death isn't painful... That is a small comfort.
Now it's your turn, Chugunov. Talk to us. I believe no lie is ever told without a reason.
I... You're right, I was lying. I happened to know that the Harbinger "Childe" and his sister Tonia managed to get tickets, so I lied to you and pretended I knew them.
And yes... I was lying about my family, too.
The truth of the matter is... I lost them... a long time ago. I just refused to accept reality. And now I've spent the second half of my life living a lie... I'm a joke.
My daughter's name was Iskra. And before you ask, yes — "Iskra" as in "Iskra Manufacturing Plant."
She... she also died from the snow cough. She was just six years old. If she were still alive today, she'd be around the same age as little Tonia here...
After Iskra passed, my wife couldn't bear to face those memories either, so she chose to start a new life without me.
One day, when I came home from work and saw the empty room, I felt like... like I couldn't breathe. Subconsciously, I started to imagine that they were still there.
I soon discovered that this was the only thing that made me feel any better, so I... I just embraced the delusion.
Nothing more than a pathetic means of escapism, I know. But at least it's not a crime.
So explain your "false testimony" then.
The night before last, when I was chatting with Tonia, she mentioned that her brother would brew medicine for her from Frostfairy Flower leaves.
Combined with her various symptoms... I suddenly understood everything, including the fact that she was deceased.
The snow cough used to be an incurable illness. I would pick Frostfairy Flower leaves to brew medicine for Iskra, too. It took hours and hours on the stove...
But the year after my daughter passed away, The Jester of the Fatui announced that a cure for Frostblight, also known as the snow cough, had finally been developed...
...It turned out that all previous treatments were completely ineffective, no better than random concoctions.
That was the final straw for me... I just couldn't take it anymore. Just one more year... one more year, and everything would have been okay!
So more than anyone, I know full well that, in this day and age, no one in their right mind would still be using Frostflower leaves to brew medicine for the snow cough...
Poor Miss Tonia, therefore, had to have been from an era when snow cough was still a terminal illness.
So, you projected your daughter onto her? Even though you knew she was one of the dead?

dialogue.sit: Even though you knew...
...That protecting her could get you killed?

dialogue.t: That doesn't make any sense. You knew she was already dead. What did you hope to achieve by protecting her?
I just... don't believe in your crackpot theories. Nor do I approve of your actions.
How can you just declare a living person dead and throw them out into that snowstorm?
Mitya's gone, my good buddy Shram's gone... and now it's "Tonia's" turn, isn't it?

The others I can make my peace with, but little miss "Tonia"... Here she is, standing right in front of us, alive and breathing, and fighting her own battles... yet you're quite happy to say she's dead...
I just want her to live... Once this snowstorm is over, the very moment it stops, I'm going to march out that door and find someone who can fetch the very best medicine for her snow cough.
I'll be damned if I'm gonna let you cast her out into the snowstorm before I have the chance to cure her!
Not again, not this time! Not when the cure is right within our grasp! I'd never be able to forgive myself!
Mr. Chugunov, stop. I can't let you do this.
Tonia...?
By the sounds of it, you've known I was dead since the night before last, right?
I really liked Mr. Valeriy, Mr. Mitya, and Miss Vodyanitsa. And now they're all dead because of me.
I'm not happy about that. The reality is, you've been trying to fight your own demons through me, but all you've really done is trap me inside your delusion along with you.
No, listen to me, I want to save you! I do!
Well, at this point, I'm quite sure that I'm dead. I don't need to be saved. The time I got to spend with all of you is more than enough for me.
Despite all the bad things that kept happening, I got to meet so many interesting people and spend so many days and nights by your side.
Since the day I escaped that hospital until now, this has been an adventure I never even dared to dream of.
I'm very fond of you all. If it were only possible, I'd trade my soul to bring back the ones who died, if it meant things didn't have to end like this...
And that's why I'm not fond of you at all, Mr. Chugunov.
...I'm sorry.
It's them that you owe an apology to, Sir. Not me.
Well then, I suppose this is it. It's time for my adventure to end. I've caused enough trouble.
You're leaving already? It's still early, don't you want to stay a little longer?
No, thank you. Oh, and by the way...
My name is Ptashka. It was nice meeting you all.
Feels strange that we're only being properly introduced now that it's time to say goodbye...
Ptashka...
What are you doing, Chugunov? Are you crazy?
Let me leave. I... I can't keep lying to myself anymore...
In your dreams. Don't think you're getting off that easy when you had a hand in the deaths of so many people...
The Fatui have honed quite an array of enhanced interrogation techniques since they were founded. Once we're out of here, Lelek will personally give you a taste of every last one...

dialogue.sit: The snowstorm continues, as if it will never stop. Nighttime soon falls once again...

dialogue.t: I think we should leave. I doubt this snowstorm is ever going to stop... For all we know, this storm might have destroyed all of Snezhnaya by now — maybe even the whole world.

dialogue.sit: I'm starting to feel the same way.
Maybe this is the heat death of the universe.

dialogue.t: Wait... We finally solved the mystery of the haunted theater today. Maybe let's at least try to enjoy tonight?
Fair enough. I don't particularly feel like dying in Chugunov's company anyway.
And yet, you won't let me die first.
Hey, Chugunov, on a serious note — if we do make it out of here, you should close down that factory of yours. A lot of people are freezing thanks to you.
Is this really the time to be discussing my factory...
Alright, fine. I'll shut it down. It doesn't matter to me anymore.

dialogue.sit: (Knock, knock, knock...)

dialogue.t: Am I hearing things? Or was that a knock at the door?

dialogue.sit: (Knock, knock, knock...)

dialogue.t: There it is again... But I don't understand. The snowstorm hasn't stopped, has it?

dialogue.sit: Maybe the snowstorm has brought us some unwanted visitors...
Or perhaps it's the rescue team that Valeriy mentioned.

dialogue.t: Should we open the door?

dialogue.sit: (Is this it? Is this nightmare finally over?)
(If the last few days are anything to go by, I probably shouldn't be getting my hopes up...)
(Whatever lies beyond that door at this moment... It could be something even more terrifying than everything we've been through so far...)

dialogue.t: ...How are you doing? Feeling any better?
Much better, thanks. Whew, it's so good to have you guys here. I was a little worried that the theater would be empty by the time I got back.
Let me see... Tonia and Vodyanitsa are missing, which means...
Vodyanitsa died last night, and then you discovered that Tonia was the other dead person. Am I right?
Not Tonia. "Ptashka."
First, tell us how you made it back here. Given the conditions outside, no one should be able to return alive.
*coughing*... You're right. The thing that got me back safely was... a song. I heard someone singing.
After walking into the snowstorm, my mind grew hazy. I don't know how long I walked through the storm before my mind completely slipped away...
Then, suddenly, I heard the sound of singing. The voice instantly brought me back to my senses, and I regained consciousness.
So I followed the voice, searching for the source of the singing. I searched and searched until finally, just a few moments ago... There was the entrance to the theater, right in front of me.

dialogue.sit: The singing...

dialogue.t: I've actually never performed this song in the theater before, because it has more of a ceremonial purpose for our people. It's not meant for the stage.
It means something like... "May those we have lost watch over us and follow this song back home in the night, so that we might be reunited once more."

dialogue.sit: That must have been Vodyanitsa's requiem... Who knew it actually worked.

dialogue.t: That song is meant to guide the souls of the dead... Mitya, that must mean that you...
No kidding... Seems like I guessed right, then. This is what I've been so desperate to tell you about.
When I first stepped out of the theater, I was still quite lucid. My memory of it is still pretty intact...

I remember the outside world being completely different than what I'd expected. It was like... this was a world where only the snowstorm existed. There wasn't a trace of any humans or buildings ever having been there.
I don't know how else to describe it, except to say that... it just didn't seem like the real world.
And as for the "requiem"... If I was guided here by Vodyanitsa's song, it can only mean that I must already be dead, and this is my soul, not my body.
But I didn't experience a clear moment of "death" while I was out there. Nor do I feel any different now than before I walked into the snowstorm.
You don't seem any different to me, either. In fact, this is something I've been wondering about for a while now... if souls aren't physical, shouldn't they lack tangible form?
Both Shram and Ptashka were clearly deceased, and yet their "souls" didn't look or feel like ghosts at all. They were visible, tangible... No different than you or me.

dialogue.sit: (This raises a truly terrible thought... Is that really what Mitya is suggesting?)
Mitya, are you trying to say that... everyone in the theater has been dead from the start?

dialogue.t: Yes. I think that... this is probably the afterlife.
What did you say?
You heard me. We died in the theater — all of us did. But due to an obstruction in the theater's Ley Lines, our souls are trapped here, while an endless, infinite snowstorm rages outside.

It's ironic, really. All that time, we were working so hard to figure out who the deceased among us were... when the truth was, we all were deceased. The only difference being, some of us died more recently than others.
Do you remember that note? "Death is near"... Seems like we misunderstood what it meant after all.
Death was nearer than we wanted to think all along. The note simply meant that all of us were already dead.
So all our attempts to survive, our search for the deceased... it was all for nothing?
Hard to say. At the very least, we helped two lost souls find clarity and go to where they belong.

The presence of those two is probably what caused our souls to be drawn in by the Ley Lines. In which case, the "deaths" we've awoken to over the past few days were just souls returning to the Ley Lines for good.
If what you're saying is true, doesn't that make us the "lost souls" now?
No wonder... This afternoon, when I was moving Vodyanitsa's body, I noticed that the other bodies in the room hadn't decayed one bit after all these days.
That's further proof that those aren't physical "bodies" at all, but merely our shells here in the afterlife.

dialogue.sit: (Am I... really dead? This doesn't feel real to me at all...)
(No, that's impossible. This cannot be how it all ends.)

dialogue.t: I still find it hard to believe that all of us are dead. How exactly did we die in the real world? None of us have any memories of dying, right?
Tch... Not even knowing how we died is preposterous. Good grief... Surely there has to be some reason?
Exactly, it's hard to rest in peace when you don't even know how you died... It gave me lots to think about as I strode out into the snowstorm.
I racked my brains, trying to remember the cause of my death, the exact moment I died, the root of all this, right up until my consciousness faded...
Wait... Hold on, right before I lost consciousness... I think I saw something...

dialogue.sit: What was it?

dialogue.t: I can't remember... Ugh, and I think I lost my notebook and pen...
Mitya, your hand... is that blood on your fingers?
Huh? You're right, there's blood on the fingertips of my right hand... looks like it's already dried. When did that happen?
What the...!?
I guess... this was what I saw? I must have desperately drawn it in my own blood right before losing consciousness...
What's wrong? Do you recognize this symbol, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: It's... Ronova. The "Ruler of Death".
Alyosha, do you still remember that Snezhnayan folk tale you told me about?
It was about the Grim Reaper. When someone's about to die, he appears as an incarnation of someone familiar to guide their soul into the afterlife.
And as soon as you recognize his face, your life is over.

dialogue.t: I heard a similar tale when I was little. You think the Grim Reaper in this story refers to the "Ruler of Death" you mentioned?

dialogue.sit: That's right. In which case, "death is near"... could also mean that the "Grim Reaper" is here, disguised in a familiar form.

dialogue.t: Haha... "Death," "the deceased," and "the Grim Reaper." So it's a triple entendre?
When I first saw this note, I thought it contradicted the investigation report. But now it seems like that was the whole intention.
So the Grim Reaper deliberately misled us... Then, we started suspecting each other and searched for the "deceased" while they hid in plain sight.

dialogue.sit: (By that logic, the one person most likely to be the "Grim Reaper" incarnate is...)
Is it you, Alyosha? You were the first to discover the investigation report, and you had plenty of time to slip the note inside to mislead us.

dialogue.t: So? Surely you can't suspect me based on that alone?
What if someone else found the investigation report first, slipped the note inside, and then put it back without telling anyone?
There's no denying it. The note could easily have been slipped in much earlier than it was discovered...

dialogue.sit: That's not all. I've also noticed that, although on the surface, Valeriy, Mitya, and sometimes I were the ones taking charge of the situation...
Looking back now, even though you didn't say much, you were always subtly guiding everyone from the sidelines.

dialogue.t: What do you mean?

dialogue.sit: You were the one who emphasized how dangerous it was outside and insisted we all stay here. It was also you who suggested that we all sleep in the same place...
And earlier today, you tried to convince Ptashka to stay... I don't understand why, but it was out of character...

dialogue.t: So... you didn't understand my intentions, and now you're assuming the worst. Seems pretty unreasonable if you ask me.

dialogue.sit: (He still won't admit it? Fine. Let's see how he responds to the most damning evidence of all...)

dialogue.t: The biggest question I have right now is... If the Grim Reaper is impersonating Alyosha, then where's the real Alyosha? When did they switch?

dialogue.sit: When all this began, right after the performance ended and the snowstorm began to pick up, no one suspected anything unusual. We just assumed we were snowed in.
It wasn't until we discovered the bodies the morning after that we realized something out of the ordinary was going on.
But it's clear now that the oddities actually started earlier than that — when Dymov walked into the snowstorm and never came back.

dialogue.t: Right, so Mr. Dymov was the first victim, not Soboleva and Torgov...

dialogue.sit: And if we pinpoint that moment as the beginning of this incident, then one thing becomes clear:
...Alyosha, you are the only person who walked into the snowstorm and came back without the help of Vodyanitsa's requiem.

dialogue.t: More precisely, Alyosha never came back at all. The one who came back... was the Grim Reaper.
Not bad. Well, since you've backed me into a corner, I suppose there's no point in keeping up the act anymore.
Alyosha...?
You're the "Grim Reaper"?
I am no such tired cliche. Mortals should address me as the "Ruler of Death."
Before being wiped out for good, you identified the two deceased and even sensed my presence... A commendable achievement. Far beyond what I expected.
I heard you can ferry souls. Those deaths each night — were they your doing?
Your initial conclusion was correct. Due to the existence of the two deceased, the Ley Lines yearned to reclaim those long-lost souls...
Every night, they devoured an equal number of souls to fill the void. This required no intervention from me — though of course, ferrying souls is indeed my authority.
Here, take a look.

dialogue.sit: O—Odette!
Mr. Chugunov!

dialogue.t: What are you doing!?
That takes care of today's two...
Don't get so worked up. You are already dead, and your souls must return to the Ley Lines.
I know we're already dead. You murdered us, didn't you?
"Murdered"? No, murder is when mortals usurp my authority. Death is my jurisdiction... If I require someone to die, I need not resort to such laborious methods as murder.
You simply met the criteria to trigger my Curse of Death.

dialogue.sit: (I know about the Curse of Immortality... So there's another death-related curse, too?)
You cursed us? When? And why would you do such a thing?

dialogue.t: So often, humans pray to me, begging to know when their death will come, and what form it will take...
But few people ask "why." If you must have an answer, know that death comes simply because one's time has come.
So you're not going to tell us the truth?
Hold your tongue. By all rights, you shouldn't even be allowed to speak with me.
Those angels from the past are to blame for their reckless renovation of the Ley Lines here. It's made my work on this occasion infuriatingly complicated.
"Work"? So trapping us here, making us watch our friends die... that's just another day at work for you?
You clearly have a lot of questions. Fine — as a reward for your remarkable accomplishments over the past few days, I shall answer a few of your inquiries, provided they aren't too unreasonable.
After the physical body dies, the soul must return to the Ley Lines for that person's "death" to be considered complete.
My work encompasses the entire process of death — including, naturally, the guiding of souls into the Ley Lines, with which you are now so familiar.
You must also be rather familiar with Natlan's Night Kingdom, I presume? It was I who supported the creation of the Night Kingdom. It provided a convenient means of guiding the souls of Natlan.
Here, too, the Ley Lines connected to the theater underwent some modifications. The angels hoped to make them capable of accommodating the souls of some special creations...
But this actually hindered their ability to accept ordinary souls to some degree.
This effect manifested itself after you died from the curse in the theater, leaving you stranded in the afterlife, unable to achieve a complete death.
But if souls who die from the Curse of Death fail to return to the Ley Lines within a short window of time, they will miss their chance for good...
Then, they will remain forever suspended between life and death, no longer subject to the authorities of either.
...So if you don't resolve this matter soon and see all of our souls returned to the Ley Lines, before long, we'll escape your control...

dialogue.sit: (Mitya is sharp. This must be what Ronova was worried might happen, and the reason she got involved to begin with.)
But if you have the authority to guide souls, why didn't you just show yourself and get it over with? Why hide among us in the form of Alyosha?

dialogue.t: You seek to understand the mind of a god? ...Hmph, very well. I'll tell you.
This is a theater, and I decided I wanted to watch a show about death. That's why I encouraged you to take the events to the stage.

I found myself getting quite immersed. I suppose the entertainment you provided makes up for all the trouble you've caused me by being so defiant in the face of death. There, are you happy with my answer?
Can't say I am.
Really? But it fits the stereotypes you humans have about gods.
Just moments ago, you were complaining about how infuriatingly complicated your work here has been.
Work is work, I get it. There are times when it's a huge pain, but you just have to get it done, right?
That's a rather unique perspective for a human... You are in fact correct. There is a pain point in this case.
Due to the obstruction in the theater's Ley Lines, there is a hard limit on the number of souls they can receive each day, making it impossible for me to ferry all your souls at once.
Revealing my identity too soon would inevitably have led to futile resistance, and there was a risk that any souls who chose to run would disappear.
Then there was the issue of the two lost souls you called the "deceased." The way you resolved that quandary was all part of my design.

dialogue.sit: That's what I don't understand. If all of us were souls of the dead, what made their presence among us special?

dialogue.t: For centuries, they have refused to return to the Ley Lines, exploiting the issues created by the angel civilization to resist being drawn in...
Centuries of obsession accumulated during this process. You may think of this obsession as the resentment of the dead, and in this quantity it was a bomb that could have detonated at any moment.

It reached the point where I could not afford to leave it unchecked. But the only way to fix it was to help them acknowledge their own deaths, make peace with their regrets, and willingly walk into the snowstorm...
Only then, with my guidance, could they finally return to the Ley Lines. Otherwise... you would not like to know what the consequences would have been.

dialogue.sit: I vaguely remember seeing... Ptashka, but in the most terrifying form. Was that in a dream? Is that what would have become of her if she hadn't returned to the Ley Lines?

dialogue.t: I see your dreams brought you many revelations... So you see, death in fact grants wisdom to mortals. Souls connect to all things in the world and see the chain of cause and effect between them. It's nothing unusual.
Anyway, giving psychological counseling to lost souls is not my strong suit...
That is more of an angel's role. It was something I could not resolve directly using my authority, so I decided it was easier to leave the "bomb defusal" to you.
Meanwhile, of course, their presence caused the souls of other members of your party to return to the Ley Lines each night... From where I stand, that was killing two birds with one stone.

As both issues slowly resolved one another without me having to lift a finger, all I had to do was stay close by and keep the situation under control. Then use my authority to wrap things up at the end.
And, of course, while I was at it... I thoroughly enjoyed watching this drama, dealing with death from a mortal perspective, play out on the stage.
Sounds like you had it all figured out, "Grim Reaper."
I just did the math. You said there's a hard limit to the number of souls the Ley Lines here can receive each day. It's two, isn't it?
That much is obvious, even to a fool.

dialogue.sit: (It's time to review this whole affair. If the Ley Lines can only take in two people per day... I need to go over the deaths from these past few days again.)
(That covers everything. It's all clear now.)

dialogue.t: Your work isn't finished yet, is it? {NICKNAME} and I are still standing here, safe and sound.
The Water Imp's song threw things off a little, but it is of no consequence.
The Ley Lines have already anchored your soul, and the first ray of light tomorrow morning will take you back. I, meanwhile, need to review my attitude towards the Water Imp race...

dialogue.sit: So the reunion in the night that Vodyanitsa mentioned... I suppose that was never meant to be a permanent reunion.

dialogue.t: That just leaves you, {NICKNAME}. My power only allows me to temporarily separate your soul from your body. The Ley Lines of Teyvat would not accept you.
And your soul is firmly anchored to your body by your will...
For a Descender like you, who is not bound by Teyvat's rules, your death can only be brought about through the most violent of means... such as directly destroying either your body or soul.

dialogue.sit: But you haven't done that yet, have you?
Thanks for letting me know that at least I can still be saved.

dialogue.t: I have no interest in involving myself with Descenders — for now. Although, this may change if Asmoday remains missing, or you insist on interfering with our affairs.
One last question, then... All our struggles and sacrifices here, they were meaningless from the very beginning, weren't they?
Death abides no reason. Besides, what you call "sacrifice" is merely a concept created by humanity.
To me, it is nothing more than a self-indulgent charade in the face of death. Mere mortals, fantasizing that their actions could reclaim something from my grasp... A truly laughable idea.

quests.description: You believed that you had solved the problem, yet the deaths continue occurring. What details have you missed? What key events have you not noticed? You continu endeavoring to leave the theater alive…

quests.title: Mistilteinn

dialogue.sit: How are you holding up, Odette?

dialogue.t: What happened to me...?

dialogue.sit: How much do you remember?

dialogue.t: Hmm? What do you mean...? Is the performance over? I can't seem to recall what happened...

dialogue.sit: (Has Odette already forgotten...?)
Mitya?

dialogue.t: Hmm...? I'm sorry, I guess I spaced out there for a second. Remind me who you are...?

dialogue.sit: Don't you remember anything?

dialogue.t: Yeah. I remember now, comrade. Looks like we guessed right.
Just like me when Odette found me at the Armory Palace... For some reason, everyone killed by the Ruler of Death eventually came back to life...
...Just with one catch: They forgot what happened while they were dead.

dialogue.sit: Odette and the others have already forgotten everything. Why were you able to remember this time?

dialogue.t: Could... this be the reason? You said this is the Ruler of Death's symbol, right?

dialogue.sit: I... I don't see anything there.

dialogue.t: You don't? Huh... Okay, I guess that makes sense. I carved this into my hand in the afterlife, so it's not visible in the physical world.
Does that mean I... carved this symbol into my soul? What an unsettling thought. Still, at least I get to remember what happened. I suppose it's a blessing in disguise.
What about you, though? The Ruler of Death mentioned that you're a "Descender," is that why you can remember?

dialogue.sit: A full explanation would get complicated very quickly, but that's essentially it.

dialogue.t: Well, then. Now that it's all over, let's figure out what we've learned.
The first thing I notice is that everything here is precisely as we left it, right before our "deaths." This confirms that time passes differently in the afterlife than in the real world.

dialogue.sit: They say that right before death, time slows down and your whole life flashes before your eyes.

dialogue.t: That must be how you know you have one foot in the afterlife by that point. Anyway, clearly the few days we spent in the afterlife probably only amounted to a few short minutes in the real world.

This also aligns with previous reports of widespread temporary memory loss among the Armory Palace personnel. Now, it seems likely that those were all brief deaths caused by the Grim Reaper's so-called "Curse of Death."
To those unaware of the truth, dying and coming back to life must feel similar to a short bout of catatonia.
This leaves me with a couple big questions. What are the conditions that trigger this so-called Curse of Death? And why are we resurrected after we die?

dialogue.sit: If nothing else, I think it shows that killing us wasn't her ultimate goal. We still don't know her true reasons for subjecting us to death.

dialogue.t: Right. This time only got complicated because of the situation with the theater's Ley Lines — that's why she had to approach it differently. If the previous incidents of amnesia among the researchers are anything to go by, killing us is usually a pretty routine matter.
Come to think of it... Wasn't I about to note something down before I "died"?
I can't remember what it was, but... I think it was something related to my research project...
Sorry, {NICKNAME}, I'll get back to you later. For now, I've got to make a trip back to the Armory Palace.
Sir(Ma'am), if I may... No one of your description has ever shown up in my investigations into Mr. Mitya's friends.
Yet you two seem very familiar with each other... Could you perhaps tell me where he was in such a rush to get to?
And by the way... have we ever crossed paths? Forgive the presumptuousness, but I feel a vague and indescribable sense of familiarity about you.

dialogue.sit: I can explain everything. Could you help me gather everyone in the theater in one place?
Everyone gathers onstage once again. But this time, you do so in the real world, without everything outside being devoured by a snowstorm.
Due to the unique properties of the theater's Ley Lines, it seems no one has completely forgotten their experiences in the afterlife.
As you recount the tale of what happened, people slowly begin to remember, as if accessing memories of a distant dream. Everyone is lost in thought...
Everyone confirms their own fate with each other, until finally today's show draws to a close.

dialogue.t: So, Chugunov really is going to shut down the factory. I guess this theater incident actually did us some good after all.
So, you said I promised to take you to the Armory Palace while we were in the afterlife, yes? I believe you. I think I even have a vague memory of it.

dialogue.sit: I want to go back and check on Paimon first...
Even though not much time has passed for her.

dialogue.t: Agreed. Let's check in on her first. The whole reason for our trip to the Armory Palace anyway is to figure out what's going on with her health.

dialogue.sit: (I'm finally back. Even though a long time has passed from my perspective, as far as Paimon's concerned, I probably just went out to watch a very short show.)
(I should keep my emotions in check when I see Paimon again, or it'll seem weird...)

dialogue.t: Wait... the atmosphere here feels off.

dialogue.sit: What do you mean?
Is there danger?

dialogue.t: Shh... Stay quiet. Let's go inside and take a look.
...Have we still not been able to notify Childe yet? We need new orders. What if that person comes back again?
Ahh...

dialogue.sit: What happened?
What were you just talking about?

dialogue.t: I'm so sorry... under the circumstances, there was really nothing we could do...

dialogue.sit: Tell me! What happened to Paimon?!

dialogue.t: I—It, it was The Jester. He came here in person and escorted Miss Paimon away.
He's the director of the Fatui. His authority supersedes all others and cannot be questioned. We... There was nothing we could do...

dialogue.sit: The Jester!?

dialogue.t: How long ago did he leave, and what was Paimon's status?
It was about an hour ago.
Miss Paimon was fast asleep at the time. The Jester simply walked off with her, as if it was only natural... I assure you, he absolutely did not use any force...

dialogue.sit: Do you know where they went?

dialogue.t: Umm...
The Armory Palace, most likely. Lord Pierro, "The Jester," has been overseeing the experiments there lately, keeping a close eye on their progress. Everyone in the Fatui has heard about it by now.
I'm surprised he came in person. Whatever his reason for taking Paimon, he'll most likely return to the Armory Palace first... which is exactly where we were headed anyway...

dialogue.sit: Then lead the way, Odette.

dialogue.t: Okay, let's go.
It's just up ahead. Quick, let's get inside...

dialogue.sit: No, I'll go alone. You know I'm planning to force my way in. You're with the Fatui, so you should stay outside.

dialogue.t: I was hardly planning on taking you through the official channels anyway. I'm here to force my way in, just like you.
I may be a Fatuus, but I'm also Lelek, enemy of Project Stuzha.
Paimon's safety is paramount right now. With me around, you'll have an extra pair of hands. There might be devices inside that are easier for an insider to deal with.

dialogue.sit: If you say so...

dialogue.t: Let's go, there's no time to hesitate.

dialogue.sit: (What's going on... Wait. I remember this feeling...!)
(It's the Curse of Death! No, no, not now! Why is the Curse of Death striking again already?)
(Odette...)
(Is this... the afterlife again?)
(I need to find a way back to reality. Is that... Odette's Cor Ignis? Could that be what just woke me up...?)
(test)台词文本
Odette... Odette!
(No signs of life, but past experience says that she should be "resurrected" before too long... right?)
(Did Odette intentionally use her Cor Ignis to guide my soul? I feel like something similar happened in a dream I had before...)
(Thank you, Odette. If not for you, my soul wouldn't have found its way back to my body so quickly, and I might not have woken up so soon...)
(But... I'm sorry. I don't have time to protect you. I have to use the time you bought me to get Paimon back!)
(Found her! Paimon really is here!)
I missed you, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Haha, what are you talking about? We haven't even been apart for that long, have we?

dialogue.sit: It was... different this time.
You seem to be in pretty good shape.

dialogue.t: Yeah, Paimon's back in tip-top condition! It's the weirdest thing — Paimon fell asleep earlier, and when she woke up, she found herself here...
The Jester and that guy talking to him used some kinda "energy" on Paimon, and she could kinda feel it canceling out that other thing that was making her feel unwell.

dialogue.sit: So, Mitya helped too?

dialogue.t: Ah, apologies for leaving in such a hurry at the theater earlier. I was in a rush to verify some theories.
Rest assured that your companion is perfectly safe. We've reversed the effects that the experimental energy had on her. The Jester specifically instructed me to do so.
I suppose this is our first official meeting, {NICKNAME}. I could not let Paimon suffer in her condition for a moment longer, and so I simply took her without explanation. I hope you do not mind.

dialogue.sit: Well, you definitely gave me a scare.
For my part, I hope you don't mind that I beat a few people up on the way...

dialogue.t: But... but why would a big shot like you care about what happens to Paimon...?
As I said when you first arrived in Snezhnaya, we once spent some time together... in the distant past.
Oh, yeah. You did mention that. And Paimon did think you seemed strangely familiar the first time we met...

I'm afraid the reminiscing will have to wait. Mitya, let us continue with the report. What conclusions, if any, did you reach from conducting the final experiment of our energy research ahead of schedule?
The good news is, my hypothesis regarding the Ruler of Death has been verified.

As for the bad news... I recommend we suspend the experiments and Project Mistilteinn until further notice. Currently, we have no means with which to make a breakthrough... I say this purely as a scientist, guided by reason alone.
I will trust your judgement. We shall put the project on hold... until the Ruler of Death has been eliminated.
Wait, wait, what are you guys talking about? You... you want to get rid of Ronova? Like, how? By killing her!?
By whatever means necessary, so long as it removes the threat she poses to us. Until then, everything we do will be in vain.
After what just happened, I've ascertained Ronova's goal... or rather, the trigger condition for the Curse of Death.

dialogue.sit: Okay, let's hear it.

dialogue.t: What she's doing is "blocking" Snezhnaya's technological progress, preventing us from possessing any means with which to threaten the Heavenly Principles.
Hmph, just like the little lapdog she is...
So, any ideas, research, or experiments that lead to technological progress can trigger the curse.
Just now, for instance, I was set to launch a final-phase energy experiment ahead of schedule. If the experiment was successful, we could have achieved a crucial breakthrough...
As expected, though, the moment the experiment began, all the researchers, technicians, and witnesses "died" from the curse.
All that effort, not to mention the energy and materials we relied on Project Stuzha to gather for us... went to waste. In the end, nothing was gained.

dialogue.sit: Does that mean something similar happened when we were at the theater?

dialogue.t: That's right. During the performance, I thought of an important breakthrough regarding the experiment, and wound up dragging everyone into this.
So the nature of the curse seems to be something like... when moments of technological progress occur, all life in the vicinity is taken away.
Wh—What a violent method...
Of course, that meant the curse was normally limited to the Armory Palace. Since outsiders are forbidden from entering, this mass-death phenomenon went unnoticed.
Until Odette came along. I believe she was the first witness. The Curse of Death was triggered just before she infiltrated the Armory Palace that day.
But you mentioned something about a "final-stage experiment"... Doesn't that mean you've actually made some progress?
That's right. Even with the gods locking certain key components out of reach, humanity can still advance technology in incremental steps accumulated over time...
But, as I'm sure Ronova anticipated, even incremental progress has its limits... a point where the "truth" you're seeking must be put to the test in an experiment.
You mean the experiment you were just about to do?

Yes, we were at a critical juncture, a moment where the quantitative was about to translate into fundamental, qualitative change. With this single experiment, we could have brought everything we've worked for to fruition.
But now, after already being forced to fumble around in the dark all this time, it feels like we've truly hit an impenetrable wall.
As long as Ronova's Curse of Death persists, we won't be able to advance the experiment or obtain any results...
And with Project Stuzha having been in effect all this time, at our nation's current strength, repeated trial and error is simply unsustainable.
Only by eliminating Ronova first will it be possible to continue advancing our plans.
But she's the Ruler of Death... She can just kill whoever she wants, right? That's gotta be the scariest power ever! Is it even possible to beat her?
We'll see. But, one thing's for sure. She definitely can't just do whatever she wants. The best proof of that is me... standing here, very much alive.
You're saying...
Wouldn't it be easier to just kill all of us researchers for good? Why resurrect us over and over again? Why let us advance our technology to this point?
So you're saying... even the Ruler of Death has limitations we don't know about?
Exactly, and I think that's where the key to our breakthrough lies.
Regardless, the "Ruler of Death" has always been an obstacle we must overcome. Indeed, we must face "Life," "Death," "Time," and "Space." After all...
...Our goal is the Heavenly Principles.
The Fatui... want to challenge the Heavenly Principles?

dialogue.sit: (For a long time, I've had a vague suspicion the Fatui and the Tsaritsa were targeting the Heavenly Principles...)
(But hearing The Jester admit it is still a shock. No wonder the Tsaritsa's goal has always been kept a secret from the people.)
(What kind of road will that lead Snezhnaya down...)

dialogue.t: In that case... Lord Jester, I would like to request some leave. I'd like some time to organize my thoughts and go over the data.
Granted. Get some rest, put the experiment out of your mind, and take care that the Curse of Death doesn't affect any civilians.
While there is yet time, allow me to offer you my hospitality, "honored guest" of Snezhnaya. Is there anything you wish to know?

dialogue.sit: About "Project Mistilteinn"...
I remember hearing the term "Mistilteinn" from Columbina.

dialogue.t: Yeah, Paimon wanted to ask about that when the name came up just now! What is it? Paimon's heard of Project Stuzha, but not this one.
As you know, Project Stuzha is a series of measures enacted to consolidate our nation's resources, the greater purpose of which... is to serve Project Mistilteinn.
Many of the things you have encountered thus far are, essentially, for the advancement of that project.

This includes the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai. Researching kuuvahki was merely a facade. Its core objective was to use local resources and research findings to build "Mistilteinn" itself...

dialogue.sit: And that's a weapon built for the final battle against the Heavenly Principles, isn't it?

dialogue.t: Huh? How did you know that?

dialogue.sit: I was given some intel, and I made some deductions.

dialogue.t: Wait... You must mean that thing over there! Oh, Paimon's gotta take a closer look at this thing. Especially after you guys sent so many people to Nod-Krai to work on it...
Kuuvahki alone will not break through Celestia's defenses, let alone challenge the Heavenly Principles.

The Heavenly Principles is no doubt accustomed to combating the power of the Light Realm. And Elemental energy is simply the power of the Human Realm, converted to that form by the Heavenly Principles themselves. Any attempt to use this power against its creator would be a futile endeavor.

For now, therefore, we have set our sights on the form of energy associated with the Third Descender and the Stellar Linchpins. This may hold the potential to allow Mistilteinn to contend with the Heavenly Principles.
You could say that by reverse engineering the Stellar Linchpins to extract the energy within, we have obtained a source of "anti-Celestia energy."

dialogue.sit: So this is the energy research that Mitya is in charge of...
I never imagined it was such a major project.

dialogue.t: The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, Project Stuzha, and the new energy experiments... So Project Mistilteinn is what ties it all together.
And it looks like your plan is almost complete... No wonder the Ruler of Death came after you...

dialogue.sit: About the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya...

dialogue.t: Her Majesty the Tsaritsa has embarked upon an expedition to vanquish a monster. Were it not for this, I imagine she would have been delighted to grant you an audience.

dialogue.sit: (Seems like the powers that be in Snezhnaya don't intend to hold my past conflicts with the Fatui against me...)

dialogue.t: The harbingers have been granted significant autonomy in retrieving the Gnoses. But by the same token, they do not completely represent Snezhnaya's official stance.

dialogue.sit: You read my mind.

dialogue.t: Speaking of the Gnoses, Paimon's been dying to ask this question since forever. Why exactly does the Tsaritsa wanna collect them? Is it something to do with the fight against the Heavenly Principles?

The Gnoses will undoubtedly serve as a key bargaining chip when she confronts the Heavenly Principles. Beyond that... you had best ask the Tsaritsa herself. I am not sure if this information is mine to disclose.
What do mean, "not sure"? Don't you make the rules? You're the highest-ranking harbinger... Ugh, never mind.

dialogue.sit: Taking on the Heavenly Principles is something most people wouldn't even entertain in their wildest fantasies. Why is the Tsaritsa so fixated on this?

dialogue.t: In Teyvat today, "civilization" is nothing but an illusion, something whose very existence can be "negated" at any moment.

Our civilization may very well be destroyed in the struggle, but as things stand, the Heavenly Principles could choose to negate our existence on a passing whim, and we must not sit back and accept that fate.
Only by changing this state of affairs, only by overthrowing the Heavenly Principles, can our civilization truly be said to have taken root...
Otherwise, the fate of the people of Khaenri'ah and Hyperborea is a cycle doomed to repeat itself.
Accepting potential destruction... in return for getting to control your own fate...
Furthermore... Hm, perhaps this is still somewhat difficult for you to understand. Are you aware that all the rules of this world are made up of "curses"?
Huh? All of 'em? Paimon knows about the Curse of Death you mentioned, and the "Curse of Immortality" that you and Dainsleif have...

dialogue.sit: Then, the birth of the Hilichurls, the rules of Natlan's Ode of Resurrection... Those are curses, too? Furina's long life seems to stem from a curse placed on her by Focalors as well...

dialogue.t: Yes... Even "a god's love for humanity" is a curse the Heavenly Principles inflicted upon the gods.
What!?
The Tsaritsa has always had ample reason to hate the Heavenly Principles...
If she can seize their authority, she will reconstruct the entire world... and when that time comes, humanity will be completely liberated from curses and lies.
Look forward to it. It will be a world beyond your imagination.

Though the ordinary people of Snezhnaya may not understand these details, in this frigid land locked in a ceaseless struggle against the environment, in this nation to which the gods have never shown favor...
We all believe that standing in solidarity with the Tsaritsa in our shared "struggle" will surely usher in a new and better world.

dialogue.sit: About your relationship with Paimon...

dialogue.t: Paimon really doesn't remember! He's basically a stranger! You've gotta believe Paimon!

dialogue.sit: Relax. You're freaking out over nothing...

dialogue.t: Allow me to explain. The reason Paimon reacted to the "Anti-Celestia Energy" developed by the Armory Palace...
...Is because she comes from Celestia herself. More specifically, she is one of its creations.
Paimon? A creation of Celestia?

dialogue.sit: (Oh right, I was blinded by anger earlier, but thinking back on it... Ronova also said that Paimon is a creation of Celestia, but she lacks Celestia's power or authority...)

dialogue.t: As you know, the lunar fragments in Nod-Krai... were "pulled" down from the sky using Fatui technology.
But, the first application of this technology was in Khaenri'ah, over five hundred years ago...
I used this technology upon the heavens, and the response I received... was none other than Paimon, descending from Celestia.
I presented her to the Vinster King, but he took no interest in this gift, nor did it satisfy him.
Paimon then took up temporary residence in my palace until, of course, the arrival of the Cataclysm.
Wait... Paimon's a little confused. You're talking about things that happened in Khaenri'ah five hundred years ago! You're saying Paimon was there for that?

dialogue.sit: That means Paimon's at least five hundred years old...

dialogue.t: But Paimon doesn't remember any of that! Falling from the sky, being given away as a gift... None of it!
Having lived through the Cataclysm, perhaps you, too, were burdened with some manner of curse, although losing your memories would indeed be the smallest price I have ever seen paid.

But it's not just her memories from Khaenri'ah... Paimon doesn't even know how she spent the last five hundred years. She only has memories from the past few years, no matter how hard she tries to remember...
What was Paimon like back in Khaenri'ah? Did she know a whole lot because she came from Celestia? Was she super smart?
Unfortunately, when you arrived in Khaenri'ah, your consciousness was like that of a newborn infant... None could say what kind of being you once were in Celestia.
During the time you lived in Khaenri'ah, your personality was no different from how it is now.

dialogue.sit: No surprise the Vinster King wasn't exactly taken by your charm.
At least it sounds like you were able to fly under the radar.

dialogue.t: Aw, man! Paimon's plan to get her memories back and become super smart is ruined before it could even start...
Y'know, even though Paimon lost her memories, she still feels weirdly close to you for some reason. That must mean you took pretty good care of Paimon back then, huh!
...On the contrary, I completely ignored your existence. I was entirely focused on my struggle against Hroptatyr "The Wise"...
But now, as I see it, it is as if you are the only sane thing that survived that era of insanity, and thus, are worthy of protection.
Uh... Noted. Man, Paimon's gotta stop projecting friendship on everyone she meets...
But, um... {NICKNAME}... E—Even though you know Paimon's some "creation of Celestia" now, you still want her right? Y—You're not going to abandon her?

dialogue.sit: You're still Paimon to me, Paimon.
As long as you're not the Heavenly Principles, we're good.

dialogue.t: Ohh, phew. That's a relief! Paimon's just learning about this too. She's barely even processed it!

dialogue.sit: I don't have any more questions. Let's talk about what's next...
Thank you for telling me so much. I'm a bit surprised, honestly. I didn't expect you to be quite so transparent with me.

dialogue.t: Given the circumstances, the Fatui need not hide anything from our allies.
"Allies"?
To advance Project Mistilteinn, we must first resolve our issue with the Ruler of Death. And, if I presume correctly... you have no intention of letting her actions go unpunished either, do you?
